FY26 CSA Financial Report 2 VIRGINIA: AT A REGULAR MEETING OF THE COUNTY OF AMELIA BOARD OF SUPERVISORS HELD AT THE AMELIA COUNTY ADMINISTRATION CONFERENCE ROOM ON WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 23, 2026. PARTICIPANTS: DAVID M. FELTS DEXTER JONES BENJAMIN MORRIS H. JOSEPH EASTER, IV TODD ROBINSON District 1 District 2 District 3 District 4 District 5 Board of Supervisors ALSO ATTENDING: ERIC S. POLLITT, COUNTY ADMINISTRATOR JEFF GORE, COUNTY ATTORNEY Chairman Felts called the September 23, 2026, Regular Meeting of the Amelia County Board of Supervisors to order at 7:00 P.M. and determined there was a quorum with all five members participating. Supervisor Morris offered the invocation, and everyone participated in the Pledge of Allegiance. APPROVE/AMEND THE AGENDA • Supervisor Morris made a request to pull Music on the Green concert from the Consent Agenda and include it under Old Business for discussion by the Board. • Supervisor Morris made a motion to amend the consent agenda with the modification of moving the Music on the Green item from Consent Agenda and adding it to Old Business as stated by Chairman Felts. Motion was approved unanimously. CONSENT AGENDA o Supervisor Morris made a motion to approve the consent agenda as amended. Motion was approved unanimously. A. Approval of Minutes • August 26, 2026 Regular Meeting Minutes B. Special Event Permit & Road Closure-Homecoming Parade C. Special Event Permit & Road Closure- Harvest Fest RECOGNITIONS None. PUBLIC COMMENTS • Mike Whitaker with Amelia County AmRev250 Committee provided the Board with information regarding the VA250 mobile museum experience on November 19th and 20th, 2026. Also, the Amelia County Historical Society is looking to get a display case for minerals to put in the county administration building. 1 • Paul White, 761 Merlin Way, discussed safety issues on the highway and VDOT’s failure to resolve things in a timely manner. Mr. White requested that a board member become active on a committee with VDOT to improve issues. • Sarah Harland discussed the late fees that are incurred when personal property taxes are not paid on time and forms are not turned into the county. Ms. Harland requested that board members remove the requirement that every taxpayer needs to return the form and to review the process currently in place. STAFF/COMMITTEE/ORGANIZATIONAL REPORTS AND PRESENTATIONS A. VDOT Report: o Adam Brooks with VDOT discussed items they are working on throughout the county. B. School Board Report: o Superintendent, Dr. Lori Harper, reported on appointed student representatives for the year, Homecoming events October 1st -3rd, and the board of supervisors facility tour on October 7th. K12 enrollment is at 1,449 and PreK12 enrollment is at 1,492. ADM for August (10 days) is at 1,412. o Financial Reports: o Director of Finance & School Nutrition, Daniel Trump, presented financial reports as of August 31st FY26. No questions were asked. o Appropriations: 1. FY26 Textbook Fund Carryover Appropriations Request (No Local Match)  $619,470.16  Supervisor Easter made a motion to appropriate $619,470.16 of textbook revenue pending mutual agreement between county finance staff and school finance staff on unaudited figures which we anticipate happening prior to next month’s board meeting. Motion was approved unanimously. 2. FY26 Cafeteria Fund Carryover Appropriations Request (No Local Match)  $728,766.77  Supervisor Easter made a motion to appropriate $728,766.77 of textbook revenue pending mutual agreement between county finance staff and school finance staff on unaudited figures which we anticipate happening prior to next month’s board meeting. Motion was approved unanimously. 3. Federal Funds Reimbursement Balances Carryover Request (No Local Match)  $566,223.76  Supervisor Easter made a motion to appropriate carryover funds of $566,223.76. Motion was approved unanimously. 4. VPSA Funds Carryover Appropriations Request (No Local Match)  $128,000  Supervisor Easter made a motion to appropriate carryover funds of $128,000. Motion was approved unanimously. o Supervisor Easter asked Mr. Trump about the consistency of what the county is reporting compared to what ACPS is reporting monthly. Mr. Trump reported that each month he reconciles with the Treasurer in terms of revenue and expenditures for the cafeteria and textbook funds and they have been aligning throughout the year. o Supervisor Robinson asked Mr. Trump whether delaying the Board’s approval of the appropriations for the cafeteria and textbook funds for one month would adversely affect ACPS. 2 Mr. Trump advised that it would impede their ability to make certain purchases due to them holding some expenditures for the appropriation. Supervisor Robinson reported that the county’s financial side is not current and more time is needed to review that to be on the same page with ACPS. Dr. Harper advised that without these funds to make purchases it will impact instruction. o Chairman Felts asked if these numbers were included in the budget for ACPS or in additional to the adopted annual budget. Mr. Trump advised that all the appropriations were in addition to their budget. C. J.L. Hamner Library Report: o Director, Keith McFarlane provided an update for the library programming. FINANCE A. Action Required Appropriations • None. B. Informational Appropriations • None. COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT A. Community Development Monthly Report • Chairman Felts asked about the termination associated with Redfield South listed under active projects on the report. William Coleman confirmed that the termination is for the storm water construction general permit. B. Environmental Department Report C. DMV Agent Compensation Statement and Payment Report COUNTY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT A. COAD Monthly Report • County Administrator Eric Politt provided a monthly report. He discussed the success of the Board Retreat on September 18th. • Supervisor Easter asked Mr. Pollitt if next month would be when the Board would receive the CIP status report and the first version of the finance summary report. Mr. Pollitt confirmed. The CIP report will be provided quarterly and revised monthly in report format. B. YTD FY26 Waste Management Host Fees • Monthly fees are $222,523.23. OLD BUSINESS A. Public Hearing-Solid Waste Ordinance Amendment | Action • Chairman Felts opened the public hearing, no one presented, and the public hearing was closed. Supervisor Morris made a motion to move to adopt the amendment to Part 1, Chapter 164, Article V, § 164-34 of the Amelia County Code of Ordinances as presented. Motion was approved unanimously. B. Public Hearing- Meals Tax Ordinance Amendment | Action • Chairman Felts opened the public hearing, no one presented, and the public hearing was closed. Supervisor Morris made a motion to move to adopt the ordinance amendment as presented. Chairman Felts, Supervisors Morris and Robinson approved the motion. Supervisors Easter and Jones opposed the motion. Supervisor Easter voted against the 3 motion as he remains opposed to adding new and additional taxes to the county citizens. C. Public Hearing- Transient Occupancy Tax Ordinance Amendment | Action • Chairman Felts opened the public hearing, no one presented, and the public hearing was closed. Supervisor Morris made a motion to move to adopt the ordinance amendment as presented. Chairman Felts, Supervisors Morris, Jones and Robinson approved the motion. Supervisor Easter opposed the motion. D. Public Hearing-BPOL Update-Short Term Rentals | Action • Chairman Felts opened the public hearing, no one presented, and the public hearing was closed. Supervisor Morris made a motion to move to adopt the ordinance amendment as presented. Chairman Felts, Supervisors Morris, Jones and Robinson approved the motion. Supervisor Easter opposed the motion. E. Music on the Green Concert |Action • Supervisor Morris stated that he was not comfortable with this event since guests may bring their own alcohol. He stated that he would be voting against it for that reason. The board discussed the concern. • Supervisor Easter made the motion to approve the event as presented and to approve the resolution to request the closure of various roads from 3:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. Chairman Felts, and Supervisors Easter, Robinson and Jones voted to approve the motion. Supervisor Morris voted to oppose the motion. NEW BUSINESS A. Committee Appointments 1. Planning Commission Nomination o Supervisor Jones made a motion to appointment Mr. Vance Anderson to the Planning Commission to fill the remainder of the term belonging to Mr. Juan Whittington of District 2, expiring on December 31, 2027. Motion was approved unanimously. 2. Library Board Nominations o Mrs. Joi Worsham presented three candidates for nomination for the Library Board, Ms. Morgan Chandler, Mr. John Holman and Ms. Takisha Bragg. Morgan Chandler with her term expiring on June 30, 2030. John Holman with his term expiring on June 30, 2029. Takisha Bragg with her term expiring on June 30, 2030. Supervisor Morris made a motion to accept all three library board nominations. Motion was approved unanimously. B. Cell Phone Tower |Discussion o Chairman Felts stated that when the tower was placed at Soapstone it was anticipated that we would make an offering to cell service to sell space. o Kent Emerson, Director of Emergency Management, presented some options to the Board for discussion. Mr. Emerson based on all the possibilities available to us that preparing our own RFP would be the best option. o Eric Pollitt, County Administrator, advised that if staff are directed to prepare the RFP in-house, the project will be deferred until the beginning of the year due to other pressing matters that he and Jeff Gore, County Attorney, are currently addressing. o Chairman Felts and the Board recommended that staff investigate the matter and develop several options for consideration at a future Board meeting. 4 BOARD MEMBERS’ COMMENTS/REPORTS District 1-The Honorable David M. Felts o Attended Piedmont Regional Jail meeting; 62 residents in August. o Retreat- good outcome o BOS Work Session on October 14, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. District 2-The Honorable Dexter Jones o Attended PSR and CRC meetings. o Receiving calls about taxes; complaints regarding late fees. o Discussion about needing ordinance change on building permits for wells. District 3-The Honorable Benjamin Morris o LAC meeting next month o Library update; committee nominations o Retreat- good outcome o Activities in county coming up; Frightfest, concert, etc. District 4-The Honorable Joseph Easter o Retreat -good outcome o Receiving calls about taxes; complaints regarding late fees. District 5-The Honorable Todd Robinson o Receiving calls about taxes; complaints regarding late fees. o Retreat- good outcome MOTION TO ADJOURN/CONTINUE MEETING o Supervisor Morris made a motion to adjourn September 23, 2026, regular meeting at 8:36 p.m. Motion was approved unanimously. text: BOARD OF SUPERVISORS WORK SESSION WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 14, 2026 6:00 P.M. AGENDA COUNTY OF AMELIA BOARD OF SUPERVISORS AMELIA COUNTY ADMINISTRATION CONFERENCE ROOM WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 14 AT 6:00 P.M. BOARD OF SUPERVISOR WORK SESSION CALL TO ORDER/DETERMINATION OF QUORUM-CHAIRMAN INVOCATION AND PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE APPROVE/AMEND THE AGENDA 1. WORK SESSION A. Financial Policies Part 1 B. Personnel Policies Part 1 C. Fire & Emergency Services Ordinance 2. MOTION TO ADJOURN MEETING COUNTY OF AMELIA FINANCIAL POLICIES MANUAL Chapter 1 ACCOUNTING & FINANCIAL REPORTING 1-1. Purpose The County of Amelia Board of Supervisors and County staff, are responsible to the County’s citizens to carefully account for all public funds, to manage County finances wisely, and to plan for the adequate funding of services desired by the public, including the provision and maintenance of facilities. 1-2. Standards The County will adhere to and maintain a high standard of accounting practices in conformance with: • Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) • The Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) • The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB); and • The Code of Virginia 1-3. Reporting A. The County will engage an independent firm of Certified Public Accountants (CPA) to perform an annual financial and compliance audit according to Generally Accepted Auditing Standards (GAAS). 1. All impacted departments are required to provide requested documentation timely by the audit team and other Department Heads. 2. Coordination may be centralized through Administration or the Finance Department. B. All activities for which the County exercises oversight responsibility are incorporated into the financial statements to form the reporting entity. C. Monthly financial reports shall be distributed to all Agency/ Department Heads by the 10th of the month for the prior month to include: 1. A Trial Balance for the prior months list of transactions. 2. A comparative report showing budget changes for prior fiscal years and the current fiscal year. 3. An overall expense and revenue report showing each starting balance, expense/revenue, and remaining balance per budget line.  Other reports available on request such as a full Year to Date expense disbursement, special funds, and other departments. D. Monthly financial reports shall be distributed to the Board and County Administrator by the 10th of the month for the prior month to include: 1. Treasurers’ Accountability Report. 2. Year-To-Date Revenue and Expenditure reports for all major operational funds and CIP fund. 3 COUNTY OF AMELIA FINANCIAL POLICIES MANUAL Chapter 2 ACCOUNTS PAYABLE 2-1. Purpose This policy describes the responsibilities and guidelines for processing expenditures incurred and disbursed for Amelia County. Accounts payable are invoices for goods and services rendered to the County for payment. The term, invoice / package, refers to the original vendor prepared bill, packing slips, receipts, and other documents as necessary that must be submitted for payment. By paying invoices in a timely and accurate manner, the County maintains good relationships with the business community. The accounts payable process ensures that expenditures by the County are for the intended purposes as authorized in the budget by the Board of Supervisors and are accurately posted to the general ledger. 2-2. Responsibilities A. Department Heads 1. Approve invoices for payment. 2. Code invoices to the appropriate budget line item that corresponds to the expenditure. 3. Submit invoices /packages to the Finance Department in a timely and accurate manner along with any supporting documentation. 4. Request new expenditure categories, within approved budget guidelines, as needed for proper coding. B. Finance Department 1. Receive invoices from Department Heads. 2. Enter new Vendor information and verify entity. 3. Review invoices for proper coding and compliance with budget. 4. Process invoices for payment. 5. Assign expenditure codes to newly requested line items. 6. Disburse payments to vendors. 4 COUNTY OF AMELIA FINANCIAL POLICIES MANUAL C. County Administrator 1. Responsible – directly or by designee - for authorizing the accounts payable registers for payment. D. Treasurer 1. Responsible for signing accounts payable registers and authorizing disbursement of funds from the bank. 2-3. Prompt Payment Act A. The Prompt Payment Act through the Virginia Public Procurement Act (§ 2.2-4347 through § 2.2-4356) requires that payments be remitted to vendors within 30 days of the receipt of: 1. 2. The vendor’s invoice, or The purchased goods or services, whichever is later. B. Most payments to outside vendors are covered by the Act. However, some vendor payments including subscriptions, honorariums, memberships, and postal supplies are not covered by the Act. Departments should allow up to seven (7) business days before the payment due date for the Finance Department to process transactions. 1. For vendor payments made by check, the postmark date shall be deemed the payment date. 2. For vendor payments made using electronic wire, the bank settlement date is deemed the payment date. This is the date the funds are deposited in the vendor’s bank account. C. Sometimes disputes occur concerning the purchase of goods and services. When a dispute occurs, the 30-day time period does not start until the dispute is resolved. Disputes can occur when: 1. There is disagreement concerning the quality or appropriateness of the goods or services received; or 2. Damaged or inoperative goods are received. D. When a dispute occurs, the reason for dispute, date resolution, and final resolution should be documented on the invoice or supporting documentation for audit review. 5 COUNTY OF AMELIA FINANCIAL POLICIES MANUAL 2-4. Internal Control The procedures should be adhered to in this policy to ensure the segregation of duties between the preparation and entry of accounts payable transactions and the approval and release of payments. 2-5. Records Retention Original expenditure documents are to be maintained in accordance with the Library of Virginia’s retention policy ensuring compliance with the Code of Virginia, or more if required by external reporting agencies. 2-6. Receipt of Invoices A. Invoices are received for coding by either the Finance Department or the Department that initiated the transaction. If the Finance Department receives the invoice, the invoice is forwarded to the initiating Department. B. Payments are made only on original invoices. In cases where an invoice has been lost, and has not previously been paid, the initiating Department must authorize payment through a payment voucher (see attached form) and attach a copy of the invoice if available along with packing slips and receipts as needed. C. Statements or listings of outstanding invoices and are never used to process payments. Statements are a tool to determine if there are discrepancies between the County’s records and the vendor’s records. D. Past due invoices received in Finance directly from the vendor will be forwarded to the initiating Department. The invoice should be stamped with all approvals within 2-3 business days so payments can be processed by Finance within the next batch. • Any late fees will be charged to the department’s budget. 2-7. Department Responsibilities for Invoices A. Each department is responsible for verifying the calculations and accuracy of invoices for payment. 1. Comparison of quantities billed on the invoice should be verified with the quantities listed on the purchase order or price quote form and shown on packing slips (receiving documents). 2. Comparison of prices, discounts, and terms should be verified with those specified on the purchase order or price quote form. 6 COUNTY OF AMELIA FINANCIAL POLICIES MANUAL 3. Proof of clerical accuracy of the invoice should be verified with respect to extensions, footings, and deductions of discounts. B. Authorized Signatories. An Authorized Signatory Form must be filled out when personnel change or personnel job duties change and is required to provide it to the Finance Department This form is signed and initialed by those individuals who are delegated with the authority to approve expenditure documents and provide disbursement transactions for processing to the Finance Department. If no personnel changes have occurred, the Department Head must submit an email to finance@ameliacova.com each fiscal year confirming that the form remains current and requires no revisions Department Heads must sign and initial the Authorized Signatory Form (see attached). C. Submission of Invoices. 1. Departments must stamp vendor invoices with the stamp furnished by the Finance Department and complete the requested information. a) Manually code the account line item to be charged with the Fund #, Major #, Object #, and amount for data entry if multiple Object #s for one invoice. (Please write clearly) b) Sign and date. 2. Each invoice needs to have a machine date and time stamped when submitted to the Finance Department. D. The initiating department is responsible for adhering to the County’s procurement policy and procedures for purchases. Approvals are required on invoices. 1. All invoices require an authorized signature or initials from the Department Head or designated signor(s), excluding monthly recurring charges such as phone, internet, utilities, etc. These invoices will be reviewed, approved, paid, and assigned to the corresponding department’s budget code by Finance and will be available for review upon request. 2. If the invoice amount is more than $5,000, Department Head approval is required. 3. If the invoice amount is more than $10,000, County Administrator approval is required. E. The invoice and any documents including packing slips and receipts should be attached and forwarded to the Finance Department for payment. F. Any department purchasing items for another department must initial approval that the service/items were received. Then the department who initiated the purchase must forward the invoice to the department receiving the service/items. Next the Department Head or 7 COUNTY OF AMELIA FINANCIAL POLICIES MANUAL designated signor for the receiving department must approve and forward the invoice to the Finance Department for processing. i. Any invoice received in the Finance department will not be paid until BOTH departments have stamped the approval. G. If the initiating department is purchasing services or goods from a vendor who has not previously conducted business with the County, then the initiating department must have vendor/contractor complete and submit an IRS form W-9, Request for Taxpayer Identification Number to the Finance Department with the invoice. The IRS form W-9 obtains the vendor’s correct taxpayer identification number, name, and address, and certifies the type of business entity. Failure of a department to obtain a W-9 form will delay payment pending receipt of form. Federal and State statutes require the County to obtain a vendor’s taxpayer identification number, Code of Virginia, Section 2.2.4354 and IRS Code, Section 3406(a). H. Reimbursement requests for travel expenses should be submitted on a Travel Reimbursement Form (see attached form) to the Finance Department no later than seven (7) business days after returning from a work-related trip. 1. Miles should be calculated from the requester’s office location to the meeting site or accommodations. A printout of driving directions showing milage is required. 2. Accommodation receipts are required. 3. Receipts are required for incidentals such as parking, tolls, food, and training materials. 4. Alcohol charges will not be covered. 2-8. Finance Department Responsibilities for Accounts Payable A. Reviews the package, including invoice or voucher supporting documentation, coding, and compliance with budget lines and County policies, for completeness. B. Confirms vendor number for existing vendor. If the vendor is new, a vendor account will be set up per the W-9 and number assigned. C. Wire or ACH instructions can be requested from a vendor and accepted if submitted on Business letterhead and verified by the Finance Director or Treasurer. D. Wire or ACH payments to a new entity requested only by email shall not be processed. E. The Treasurer or Chief Deputy Treasurer must approve first time or non-repetitive wire or ACH requests. The Finance Department coordinates with Treasurer’s Office for processing of wire or ACH payments. 8 COUNTY OF AMELIA FINANCIAL POLICIES MANUAL F. Changes requested electronically by county staff must be verified in person by the Finance Department. Request for changes to bank or wire instructions shall not be accepted via email only. Any requested changes to vendor information must be verified with an existing known contact either by phone using a pre-existing phone number, or fax using a pre-existing fax line associated with the vendor. G. Verify that the required approvals have been obtained. If required approvals have not been obtained, will communicate with the Department to coordinate approval and receipt within 2-3 business days to avoid payment delays. H. If the package is deemed not complete in accordance with this policy, the Finance Department will work to resolve the problem. If a resolution is not successful within 2-3 business days the package will be returned to the Department for further resolution. I. Data is entered into the computer system for generation of the checks, after review and correction or clarification of any information. J. The Director of Finance reviews, edit reports, and invoices for accounts payable prior to posting to the general ledger and printing checks. K. A Check Register is prepared for approval by the County Administrator or designee for payment of checks. L. An Accounts Payable Reconciliation Report is prepared for authorization by the Treasurer or designee for checks to be paid from the bank. 2-9. Manual Checks When absolutely necessary, a manual check may be written. A request must be made in writing with the reason for a manual check to the County Administrator for approval. 2-10. Check Writing Schedule Invoices received by Wednesday each week will be processed within that week’s batch if the package is complete. Any complete packages received after close of business Wednesday will be processed in the following week’s batch. (Shorter weeks due to Holidays or other closures may have a small delay). Invoices are generally paid every Friday, except on weeks with holidays. 2-11. Uncleared and Voided Checks A listing of uncleared checks shall be generated by the Treasurer monthly. Accounts payable checks outstanding 60 days should be reviewed by Finance, and contact should be made with the vendor to confirm receipt of the check. Checks not received by the vendor shall be voided 9 COUNTY OF AMELIA FINANCIAL POLICIES MANUAL in the accounting system, a stop payment request shall be issued by Finance to the Treasurer who will initiate stop payment with the bank, and the payment reissued by Finance. If contact is unsuccessful and the check remains outstanding after 90 days, the check shall be considered stale dated and voided in the accounting system and payment shall not be reissued. o Checks mailed within the state will not be reissued until at least 14 business days have passed from the mailing date unless a known address error exists. o Out-of-state checks will not be reissued until at least 30 business days have passed unless a known address error exists. o If a second check is issued and not received, a third check will only be available for inperson pickup. o For out-of-state recipients, a third check shall be mailed using signature confirmation, and any additional postage costs may be charged to the recipient. o Electronic payment methods may be used when feasible. Voided checks must: o Be properly documented o Include reasons for void o Be approved by the Finance Director or designee Reissued checks must reference the original check number. 2-12. Reclassification of Accounts Payable after Payment If a department determines that a paid invoice has been incorrectly coded and/or posted to a budget line item, the department must contact the Finance Department to reclassify the cost within two (2) months of the date posted in the general ledger. At the end of the fiscal year (June 30th), any reclassifications must be requested within 45 days after year-end. An end of the fiscal year aged budget change request will be accepted for review by Finance as long as it is done within 45 days of the fiscal year’s end and all requests are received within one email outlining the vendor name, amount, date, invoice number, original budget allocation and the needed changes (see attached excel sheet as an example). 2-13. Fiscal Year End Cut-Off Procedures At the end of March each year, fiscal year end cut-off procedures will be distributed to departments outlining deadlines for purchases and invoice payment schedule. 10 COUNTY OF AMELIA FINANCIAL POLICIES MANUAL Chapter 3 CHECK SIGNING 3-1. Procedures A. Checks are processed by the Finance Department and forwarded to the Treasurer’s Office for signatures. B. Checks are required to have all the proper documentation attached to the checks to be signed, including a check register report showing the check number, payee and dollar amount. The sheet that shows the batch and the amounts for each fund that will affect the general ledger must also be attached. C. All documentation related to online and ACH payments must be provided to the County Administrator or Deputy County Administrator, and the Treasurer within 24 business hours of payments being made. D. The County Administrator or Deputy County Administrator signature must be included on the check register report indicating approval of the checks. E. The Treasurer’s Office will review and approve the summary sheet that shows the batch and the amounts for each fund that will affect the general ledger. F. Checks presented with changes/corrections to the name or amount will not be signed. G. The Treasurer’s Office has the authority to refuse to sign checks without the proper approvals or documentation. H. All voided checks must be delivered to the Treasurer’s Office to be properly identified in the general ledger as a voided check. It is important that this procedure is followed in the same month the checks are voided. I. The Treasurer is responsible for placing all stop payments on checks through the bank. J. Payment for vouchers/bills will not be remitted by giving the county’s account number or check number over the phone. NO ONE EXCEPT THE TREASURER HAS THE AUTHORITY TO GIVE OUT THE COUNTY BANK ACCOUNT NUMBER TO A VENDOR OR APPROVE A VOUCHER/BILL BY PHONE OR WIRE. 11 COUNTY OF AMELIA FINANCIAL POLICIES MANUAL Chapter 5 PURCHASING & PROCUREMENT The County is subject to and shall comply with the Virginia Public Procurement Act (Va. Code §2.24300 et seq.) for the purchase of all goods and services covered by the Act. Pursuant to Va. Code §2.2-4303, the County adopts the following Small Purchase Policy: General: The Virginia Public Procurement Act permits a locality to establish written small purchase procedures for purchases from non-governmental contractors and vendors that do not require competitive sealed bids or competitive negotiation, on the condition that such procedures provide for competition wherever practicable. Section 2.2-4303(G) Code of Virginia, 1950, as amended. In general, the objective of this policy is to provide the County and its taxpayers with the best value possible - reflecting high quality and best price - through efficient and effective use of the competitive market, when practicable, in compliance with the Virginia Public Procurement Act. 5-1. This inspector will monitor compliance with stormwater management and vegetative buffers, with any violations prompting an immediate stop-work order. 6. The "Chain of Title" Liability: Ensure that all Special Exception Permit conditions, noise limits, and decommissioning bond liabilities automatically transfer to any future owner or parent corporation. If a subsidiary or shell company dissolves, the primary energy entity remains legally and financially responsible to Botetourt County. 7. Forbidding the use of Chemical and Herbicides: Restrict the use of chemical defoliants for site maintenance to protect karst groundwater and local wells from runoff. Lounge: To prevent noise from carrying throughout the area, and especially to nearby residential uses, the doors and windows shall be kept closed except as patrons enter and exit. If the current use of the property as a Lounge or Golf Course, ceases for more then two (2) years, this Conditional Use Permit becomes null and void. 15. A building permit is obtained for the business sign prior to approval from the Brunswick County Board of Supervisors. Adjournment Buckingham County Planning Commission September 28, 2026 At a regular session of the Buckingham County Planning Commission held on September 28, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in the Peter Francisco Auditorium located in the Buckingham County Administration Complex, the following members were present Ashley Shumaker Chairman: James D. Crews III Vice-Chairman; John Bickford, DJ Anderson; Joyce Gooden; Calvin Bachrach, Cameron Gilliam and Steve Dorrier. Also present were Cheryl T. “Nicci” Edmondston, Zoning Administrator and E.M. Wright, Jr., County Attorney. Re: Call to Order The Planning Commission meeting was called to order. Re: Invocation and Pledge of Allegiance The invocation was given by Commissioner Dorrier. The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Bachrach. Re: Establishment of a Quorum Shumaker: We have approval of the agenda. Miss Edmondston, I believe we are going to move public comment back to its normal position after approval of minutes and before old business. All right. With the amended agenda, could we get a motion? Crews: So moved. Bickford: Second. Shumaker: Have a motion and a second. There's no discussion. We'll take a vote. Unanimous eight of eight to approval of minutes from our regular monthly meeting on August 24, 2026. Are there any changes or edits to be made? Seeing none, do we have a motion? Bickford: Motion to approve as presented. Gooden: Second. Shumaker: Have a motion and a second. Any conversation? Take a vote. Right, unanimously approved. And now we'll move into public comment. Commissioner Yay Anderson X Crews X Dorrier X Bickford X Shumaker X Gooden X Bachrach X Gilliam X Nay Commissioner Bickford moved, Commissioner Gooden seconded and was carried by the Planning Commission to approve minutes as presented. Edmondston: Yes, this evening we have 21 individuals signed up to speak. The first will be Joseph Anthony, followed by Donnie Duke. Joe Anthony: Hello, my name is Joe Anthony. I live at 3977 Oak Hill Road, right here in District Four. Thank you for taking my comments regarding the preferred corridor designation in the proposed amendment to the Buckingham Comprehensive Plan, I'm urging you all not to adopt it. It weakens Buckingham at every level at a time when we need to stand strong against data BUCKINGHAM COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION September 28, 2026 2 center. Infrastructure that will destroy what we love here. Don't undo the county's strong opposition to Valley Link with this amendment. Thank you, Shumaker: Mr. Anthony did a great job. But sorry, I'll remind everyone to state your name and address, and everyone will have three minutes. Edmondston: Donnie Duke, followed by Nico Anderson. Donnie Duke: Donnie Duke, District Five, 564 Unity Place, Buckingham. Talking about power lines, data's right of way. Whatever our forefathers say, our forefathers fought over the owners of the Indians. Eminent domain was the name this callous took. Eminent domain plagues us now-a rifle in the sky. I'm not branding iron. I don't protest your right to vote. I'm not going to just call you evil, play hippie songs, and pretend we're in the '60s. Look at that good and evil. I have not been coached on what to say, sin fathers. If you go by another name, I'm sorry, I am not gender confused. We're dealing with power structures here, and a land grab, patriarchal pudding and pie. May I have your attention. This is not all she wrote. It's eminent domain, ladies and gentlemen, coming upon our land and taking our property, digging in on American soil to take our privacy from us, to steal our certain right-the right to own and share private property, and we speak of the American way. Fine, you need a railroad, and railroads are far and few and far between. You need some land for the military, and you're at war. Or you need a country county road, a state highway, and we can just suck it up for the need. The need is truly great. You're skinny dipping on land that's not yours when you cut us to pieces for a shareholder's price. You take our land for profit. Is that public need? I bid you. It's not. Can I get a scorecard? We want to tally right and wrong. We want you to sit in your breeches or flowery skirts and say how you're the righteous among us, those who follow God, well, show us this, please, by not taking private property for to make money, the eminent eminent domain. Edmondston: Nico Anderson, followed by Britton Doherty. Nico Anderson: Hello, members of the Planning Commission. Hi, everyone. My name is Nico Anderson. I live at 330 Liberty Lane in Buckingham, in District Five. So I understand what this what this amendment is trying to do. The stated goal is to keep a new transmission line from cutting through the interior of Buckingham. That's the goal everyone in this room shares. But I want to point out what the amendment actually commits this county to do. Section five says that when a utility proposes a line outside of the preferred corridors, the county will go to the state corporation commission and submit evidence that the preferred corridors can adequately serve the company's needs. Under state law, that evidence is the county's to bring. Here's the problem: the county has never studied these corridors to see whether they could even work. No study of whether they could carry a line like Valley Link has been presented to the commission. The amendment itself keeps saying where engineering feasible, because that work has not been done. So the county would be committing to prove something it has never checked and paying engineers, experts, and attorneys to find out. Think about what this means with Valley Link. The current routes are new routes across new ground. Under this amendment, the county would be committed to arguing that the line should go somewhere else instead, somewhere BUCKINGHAM COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION September 28, 2026 3 along the northern corridor to the James River side, along the eastern corridor, along our highways, or across cleared farmland. In other words, the county would be arguing. To put a 765 kilovolt line within its own residence land, this county has committed up to $250,000 to oppose ValleyLink. Under this amendment, that money would go could end up funding an argument about where the line should go, instead of an argument about what should about that it shouldn't come at all, and that families along those corridors pay the same taxes that would fund it. Opposing a line and redirecting it are not the same thing. The amendment turns the county's opposition into a relocation plan that weakens our hand against Valley Link today and against every utility that comes after it. Please, please keep the county's opposition what it was meant to be. Please recommend that the preferred quarters amendment not be adopted. Thank you all for all of your time and service. Edmondston: Britton Doherty, followed by Doug Mcillanie. Britton Doherty: Hi all. Thank you for your time. My name is Britton Doherty. I live at 330 Liberty Lane in District Five. My comment is in regards to the Preferred Corridors Amendment. My question for you all is: Why should proximity to an existing transmission line outweigh the county's existing land use objectives concerning farms, water, conservation resources and residential communities. The preferred corridors amendment is in direct opposition to the county's existing land use objectives, and the real question is who benefits from that and who loses. Virginia Code 15.2 dash 2223 says the planning commission is supposed to study existing conditions, future requirements, and the needs and resources of the territory, with the objective of objective of promoting health, safety, prosperity, and general welfare of the inhabitants. Does this amendment serve the inhabitants of this county. If you want to invest in technology infrastructure for residents and businesses, Virginia law expressly tells comprehensive plans to consider broadband infrastructure sufficient to meet the future needs of residents and businesses. This would directly serve homes, farms, and local businesses throughout Buckingham before Buckingham commits public resources or tax incentives to infrastructure intended to primarily attract high-energy industrial development, they could be investing in broadband expansion, volunteer fire and emergency response capacity, schools and vocational training, road bridge improvements, water and wastewater systems, affordable housing, agricultural preservation, local farm infrastructure, and locally owned small business development, and many other things. Thank you all so much. Edmondston: Doug McElaney then Santoshi Young will be next. Doug McElhaney: Good evening. My name is Doug McElhaney. I live at 564 Unity Place in District Five. County staff wrote 14 questions for this commission to work through before deciding on this amendment. None of them has been answered. In June, this commission tabled this amendment so it could study it further, including its effect on conservation easements. This July work session was set for that purpose. It ended without any direction. Today, all 14 of those questions are still unanswered. Our own comprehensive plan quotes Virginia law: when preparing a plan, this commission shall make careful and comprehensive surveys and studies. The study this commission asked for still hasn't happened. The options BUCKINGHAM COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION September 28, 2026 4 matrix prepared for that same work session is also cut off. Pages are missing or improperly formatted, so commissioners have only been able to see part of the choices they were asked to weigh. A decision this important shouldn't be made from an incomplete set of options, and the amendment itself is full of gaps and inconsistencies. The key words parallel and adjacent have no defined distance. Its preferred list includes cleared agricultural land. In plain terms, that means working farms and conservation easements and homes appeared nowhere on its list of places to avoid, every one of those gaps leaves this county vulnerable, and these aren't problems a few edits can fix. They show an amendment that is specific about what the county is willing to give up, and silent about some of what it most needs to protect. There are 14 unanswered questions. There has been no study. The options matrix is incomplete, and there are undefined terms and inconsistencies throughout. This amendment isn't needed, and an amendment this flawed with this many vulnerabilities should not be recommended to the board. Please recommend that the preferred corridors amendment not be adopted. Thank you. Edmondston: Santoshi Young, followed by Chad Oba. Santoshi, is not here. Okay, Chad Oba, followed by Jiva Abate. Shumaker: They just sent someone. They thought the public comment was later on the agenda. No, ma'am. You can go ahead. Thank you. Gooden: The sign-up time is still the same, isn't it? Shumaker: I believe they made it onto the sheet. They’ve properly signed up, but they thought the based on the published agenda that the public comment was later in the night. Okay, Gooden: So they signed up, or does somebody else sign up for them? That's my question. Edmondston: Santoshi signed Chad Oba: First of all, sorry, Chad Oba, District Six. First of all, thank you to this commission for taking the time to not rush through this and to really study it, I really appreciate that it's an important thing to consider, and I also appreciate your change to the agenda tonight to put the public comments at the beginning. I think many people, the people that came to speak tonight, really appreciate that. I know I do. Public comment is vital to the democratic process. It is one of the few direct avenues for individuals and community stakeholders to influence official policies and regulations before they take effect. It can provide valuable points of view and information that you could find helpful in making decisions, and has the potential to increase trust between you, our representatives, and the community. I like to think of it as a productive, but necessary and sometimes discomfort. So here are my comments regarding the utility quarter amendment, a family living beside an existing power line in Buckingham could go from a 70-foot tower to one more than twice that tall, and a corridor three times as wide. Many existing lines in this county sit in rights way of around 100 feet, with towers around 70 feet tall, Valley Link's own materials put typical 765 kV towers at around 150 to 175 feet on a right-of-way of about 200 feet. Put the new line beside the old one, and 100-foot corridor becomes closer to 300 feet. That's triple the BUCKINGHAM COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION September 28, 2026 5 width of land taken out of a farm, a pasture, or a family's backyard. That's like the two-lane country road in front of your house being turned into a divided, multi-lane interstate. Many of these families never asked for the first line. It came decades ago, often before the people living there now, they've lived with that burden ever since. This amendment would mean the burden would be compounded, and no one has studied these existed corridors. It doesn't stop at one line either. How many more would be added on? It's a compounding burden on the same families forever. Buckingham should never be a county that sacrifices any of its own families. What we choose to protect says a great deal about what we value. Please protect our families, our land, our beautiful county of Buckingham. Thank you. Edmondston: Madam Chairman, would you like to have Santoshi Young speak? She’s back in the room now, followed by Jiva Abate. Shumaker: Okay. We'll put her at the end after the remaining public comment. Jeeva Abate: I'm Jeeva Abate, District Five, live at 12 Rama Lane in beautiful Buckingham County. So I'm going to address The Utility Corridors Amendment, and I started to write for my analysis, and I realized I look out my window and I'm in a forest, and I love Buckingham. I love the land, the water, our air, and our neighbors. So because of that, I look at this Valley Link project, and I'm concerned. And this whole project's gotten intense pushback from residents, farm owners, landowners, and the Buckingham County Board of Supervisors. One of the main issues is that the Constitution allows for eminent domain seizure when that project supports the public good. This does not support the public good. It supports the data centers, the billionaires who build the data centers, and the billionaires who are building AI, who are now telling us, give us a moratorium on AI. So this is a concern when the people who built this are telling us we have a problem, we have a real problem. The easements restrict how owners can use their own property if eminent domain is exercised. We lose land value and marketability with one of these giant structures on our farms or property. There's economic and agricultural impacts where I come from, Yogaville. We have a active farm. It's a part of what we offer, and now you've got clear cutting, you've got prime soil and tracks divided. It's not good. You've got environmental and viewshed destruction. So when you go out and you want to look at that beautiful mountainside, now you see all these huge towers, and then there's the public health and safety, which, since I've given you all my report, you can look at the diagram, which was submitted to the Texas Public Utility Commission by the Texas utilities themselves, so they've done this research. The constant exposure to EMF is connected to higher human and animal disease rates. There's incidence of childhood leukemia within 900 feet of the center line. A Swiss study found elevated dementia and Alzheimer's mortality. Human reproductive efforts are impacted, and increased breast cancer. Shumaker: That's the end of your three minutes. Thank you. Edmondston: George Goodwin, followed by Ruth Olinger Aldridge. BUCKINGHAM COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION September 28, 2026 6 George Goodwin: Name is George Goodwin, District Six, Belle Meade, Scottsville. I had a speech tonight, but I'm not going to even give it. You've heard my comments, and I believe you all know what my position is, but let me explain. Our position is we have followed the county's comprehensive plan. We came to you for Airbnb, came to you, and were approved, thankfully, and we operate very well. And with all within all the rules, you receive more taxes from us because of that, and a lot of tourism dollars. We came to you with promoting tourism on the river. You proved that, and it's been very successful as well. We're still trying to follow that. You asked everybody to particularly promote conservation easements, if you provided a designated corridor over a particular our property, and amongst lots of other people, when you're talking about this, but I'm I'm asking about myself tonight, and I will be prohibited. You pass this. Would be one more thing that I would be prohibited from doing another set of handcuffs, because you're not following the comprehensive plan if you designated that. So I beg you, you look at our property. We have seven utility easements on the property. That's 38% of my land cannot be accessed successfully. I asked Appalachian Power permission to drill a well 80 feet below the tower line. 80 feet. The rig was only going to go up 42 feet, but they wouldn't allow it. I had to. I'd paid a geologist, county geologist that used to work here, to tell me where the best places were. Two of them were under the power line. I had to go for option three. Those are just more and more restrictions, and if they put another 200 foot easement right beside the one without any buffer in between them, the line would the utility corridor would be 76 feet from one of my buildings, and it's a dwelling, not just a building. I ask you to seriously take a look at what you're considering, and vote no. Thank you very much. Edmondston: Ruth Olinger Aldridge, followed by Kenda Hunnaman. Madam Chairman, Santoshi back. So, do we still move her to the end of the comments? Shumaker: Yes, I think we'll move. Is it is that okay? Thank you. Ruth Aldridge: This is a medical device. I'm Ruth Olinger Aldridge, District 6286, Hummingbird Road, Scottsville, Buckingham, approximately seven miles from the James River Waterway to the Chesapeake Bay as the water flows. My biggest concern and has been will remain to be water. I've attended prior county meetings and have shared my concerns. Now I'm here to speak ever more with the Technology Overlay District about water, especially drinking water. As a newly diagnosed patient of a tick bite from the woods of our home over 20 years that we call home, a diagnosis of AFAGAL, the meat allergy, a diagnosis that partially paralyzed the right side of my face for over a month and a half. A now side effect in which I now cannot have bottled water that is not filtered through chard, which is a bone processing system to purify water for drinking consumption. That's because … COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION September 28, 2026 9 if it goes through a 2000 acre solar farm on the low end, will generate at the low end 10s of millions of dollars per year, 10s of millions of dollars a year for the next 40 years, and we got … One names places the county prefers for new high voltage lines. The other names places the county wants to avoid. On paper, this sounds balanced, but read them side by side, and they run straight into each other. One of the first choice … It prefers cleared farmland for high voltage lines. It leaves conservation easements and family farms off its list of places to avoid. And it would not add a new transmission quarter objective under Goal Nine, the plan's goal to conserve … I would anticipate an introduction at the October meeting for your zoning map amendment, a public hearing in November, introduction to the Board of Supervisors in December and January, the final public hearing. This is tentative … The B1 taking the zoning map amendment would eliminate those. So this is going to give you a very. If the zoning map amendment is approved, you would have matching zoning to where you are currently. So we would not be discussing your … As far as SUP versus zoning map amendment. It does require new application. The SUP process is now at the December timeline. If we were to take a zoning map amendment, it would be a January, as following a tentative four-month process … / Dillwyn Metalworks BUCKINGHAM COUNTY, VIRGINIA Planning Commission Staff Report Rezoning — Zoning Map Amendment Case No. 26-ZMA371__ - Randy Waycaster — Dillwyn Metalworks Marshall Magisterial District - Tax Map 126, Parcel 10 - A-1 to … recommends that the Planning Commission forward a recommendation of APPROVAL OF THE REZONING FROM A-1 TO M-2, INDUSTRIAL DISTRICT – HEAVY, AS APPLIED FOR, for Case No. 26-ZMA371__. VALLEY LINK PROJECT ROUTE OPPOSITION At the September 1, 2026, meeting of the Board, Supervisor Cline asked, with the concurrence of the Board, that staff prepare a resolution of opposition to the proposed Valley Link Transmission Line route. The proposed Valley Link transmission line would include the construction of a 765-kilovolt (KV) transmission line extending from Campbell County to Culpeper County, Virginia. The project has engendered significant opposition, and each locality along the proposed route, with the exception of Campbell, has taken action to convey its opposition. The final route has not yet been submitted to the State Corporation Commission (SCC) for approval. Any Board action on this topic would be an expression of concern that would inform the SCC’s deliberations over the proposed route, but the Board does not ultimately have any control over the line as a land use determination. Said differently, the County does not control the route via zoning. In response to the inclusion of this item on the agenda, five (5) individuals contacted County Administration in accordance with our protocol and asked to be placed on the agenda to address this topic. Rather than include them separately and apart from this action item under appearances, they are included here so that the Board may receive their input in conjunction with your consideration of the agenda topic. Those speakers, in the order in which their requests were received, are: 1. Rick and Cheryl Summy 2. Becky Nix 3. Meghan Leatherwood 4. Shelly Evans 5. Rob Mann RECOMMENDATION: Staff requests the Board’s consideration of the attached resolution. BOND FINANCING - ALTAVISTA COMBINED SCHOOL Since 2019, the County has worked with Davenport Financial Advisors to develop a Strategic Plan of Finance. Since that time, the County has proceeded with the construction of Rustburg Middle School, the implementation of the Regional Radio System, the renovation of Brookville High School, and the construction of a 100,000square-foot shell building for economic development. The next school capital project to be undertaken is the Altavista Combined School. At the Board of Supervisors’ July meeting, the Board authorized staff to proceed with the project at a total cost not to exceed $45 million. Since that authorization to proceed, School Division staff secured a state construction grant in the amount of $13.5 million to offset some of the costs associated with the project. Because the County received the benefit of the Commonwealth grant funding, Davenport was asked to evaluate the financing scenarios that reflect the potential reduction in borrowed funds, as well as an option to incorporate financing for a Public Safety facility to be located at Yellow Branch. That analysis is attached for your review and consideration. To summarize: 1. Scenario 1 includes borrowing $42.5 million, to be used in conjunction with $2.5 million in available funding to generate the total $45 million school fund without grant funds. 2. Scenario 2 includes borrowing $29 million to be used in conjunction with the $2.5 million in available funding plus the $13.5 million construction grant to fund the total $45 million school project. 3. Scenario 3 includes borrowing $39.5 million. This would include borrowing $29 million for the school project (to be used with the state grant of $13.5 million and available funding of $2.5 million) plus another $ 10.5 million for a public safety facility. The results of the analysis are summarized in a table found in the attached memorandum. RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends the Board determine which strategy is preferred and adopt the required bond resolution in such amount as is required and to authorize staff to execute all necessary documents. BOARD OF EQUALIZATION APPOINTMENTS The required four-year general reassessment of real property is underway, and reassessment notices will be mailed to property owners the week of October 26, 2026. Property owners who disagree with the results of the reassessment can request an office hearing with the assessor. Most issues are resolved at the office hearing stage; however, owners who still wish to contest their assessment may request a hearing with the Board of Equalization (B.O.E.). The B.O.E. has the statutory authority to adjust and equalize the assessments. Members of the B.O.E. are appointed by the Circuit Court, but the Court typically relies on recommendations from the Board of Supervisors. The B.O.E. will meet as needed between January 18, 2027, and March 5, 2027. Members are required to attend a brief training session provided by the Virginia Department of Taxation before undertaking their duties. The Commonwealth of Virginia requires localities to have at least three (3) members on the B.O.E., and Campbell County customarily utilizes a three-member board. All members are required by law to be citizens of Campbell County and “broadly representative of the community.” A majority of members must also be property owners, and at least 30% of members must be professionals in the fields of real estate, development, construction, law, or finance. It is recommended, but not required, that members of the B.O.E. be retired, self-employed, or otherwise in control of their own schedule. In order to ensure a quorum is present, it is very important that members are consistently available for meetings on various weekdays and evenings while the B.O.E. is active. The previous Board of Equalization consisted of Donald R. Leslie (Crossroads Lane, Evington), William T. Burleigh (Booth Road, Concord), and J. Michael Davidson (Sugar Hill Road, Brookneal). The Board does not answer questions nor establish dialogue during the Public Comment period. Please approach the podium when called, state your name, and any relevant facts or materials. Written comments and documents may be submitted for the record. Key Issues Raised by Citizens Pat Davis Pat Davis urged the County to eliminate data centers as a by-right use and narrow their zoning definition, drawing on other counties’ experiences. She expressed concern that by-right approval allows overly broad industrial development and stated that it contributed to the County’s current issues involving Point One. Brandi Marano spoke on behalf of several absent residents from the Brentwood Estates and Old Union areas. She questioned the approval of legal expenses without supporting documentation and whether more affordable representation had been considered. She called for greater transparency regarding DEQ consent orders and wastewater projects and urged review of data center actions for consistency with the executive order she referenced. She also raised concerns about the canceled BZA hearing, alleged errors in member appointment procedures, and the County’s awareness and disclosure of data center turbine and generator details. Jackie Stewart encouraged residents to remain engaged and expressed hope that future Board membership changes could lead to reconsideration of current decisions. She raised concerns about recurring financial audit issues and urged continued community participation. Identifying herself as an at-large candidate, she announced that she would be at the library Saturday at 11 a.m. to hear residents’ concerns. Thelma Whitehead, speaking on behalf of a group, questioned the County Attorney’s role and whether separately retained legal representation should be Mr. Adkins’s personal responsibility. She expressed concern about Mr. Patterson’s reported difficulty obtaining timely information and called for accountability. She also questioned approval of legal expenses without clear, itemized documentation and stated that residents would continue challenging the decision. Bill Hopke speaking on behalf of a group, questioned the proposed $53,350 payment of Mr. Adkins’s legal fees and stated that dismissal of the removal proceeding left residents’ underlying concerns unanswered. He requested the County Attorney’s clarification regarding Mr. Adkins’s potential personal interest and eligibility to participate in the vote. He also requested written certifications from supervisors supporting reimbursement concerning their knowledge of conduct affecting County finances and documented efforts to recover or reconstruct financial records unavailable to the forensic auditor. He emphasized transparency and accountability when using public funds.. Robert Tyler, speaking on behalf of a group, criticized legal expenditures related to Mr. Adkins and alleged that the County obstructed the forensic audit and improperly destroyed supporting records. He raised concerns about land transactions, undocumented food pantry expenditures, the accounting of COVID funds, and discrepancies involving the Market 5 contract, container delivery, and payment transfers. He supported ending the audit, stating that he believed the available findings warranted a criminal investigation. Lloyd Carter raised concerns about proposed lithium battery storage at solar facilities, including fire response plans, containment measures, and potential contamination of local waterways. He urged the County to prioritize residents’ safety and revisit water-monitoring requirements associated with solar project approvals. He also requested information about property reassessments and potential tax impacts and called for accountability regarding County affairs. 6 of 69 John Manning stated that online commentary prompted his attendance and expressed concern about what he viewed as character attacks. He indicated that he accepted the judge’s decision because the allegations had not been proven in court. Martha Harris speaking on behalf of a group, opposed payment of Mr. Adkins’s legal fees, questioned his participation in the vote, and requested clarification about potential insurance reimbursement. Citing reported staffing-related closures at Fire Station 3, she raised concerns about emergency response times and spending priorities. She also described residents’ concerns about grinder pump placement and safety in the Mt. Zion sewer project, questioned the proposed transfer of the schools’ wastewater treatment plant amid County compliance issues, and called for continued efforts to account for financial matters raised by the forensic audit. Preston Adkins expressed disappointment with the decision regarding the schools’ treatment plant, citing past DEQ violations during County management and subsequent improvements under school oversight. He urged the County to prioritize reliable service and regulatory compliance, noting that a water outage could force school closures. He also questioned the County’s record of completing projects successfully. Jared Kline questioned the consistency of public comment time limits for group representatives and urged the County Administrator to take responsibility for addressing longstanding issues. He recommended presentations and supporting documentation to inform Board decisions and improve public transparency. He also questioned Mr. Hill’s vote given concerns about incomplete information and encouraged Board members to make motions addressing spending concerns and unanswered questions. Board Member Hill: Board Member Hill stated that he strives to treat everyone equally and bases his votes on available evidence, the law, and his conscience. He explained that he had not been presented with evidence of illegal conduct and would vote differently if such conduct were established. He acknowledged residents’ differing opinions and emphasized that he takes his responsibilities seriously. Chairman Adkins: None at this time.
