text: Updated 10/23/26 FRANKLIN COUNTY ZONING ORDINANCE UPDATE DRAFT ARTICLE 3 – PERMITS & APPLICATIONS l MARCH 26, 2026 ARTICLE 3. PERMITS AND APPLICATIONS1 DIVISION 3-1. IN GENERAL.2 If an applicant seeks both an amendment to the Zoning Ordinance and a Special Use Permit for the same property, both applications may be made jointly and processed at the same time if the proposed amendment does not add a conditional use not previously permitted by the terms of this Ordinance. Section 3-1-1. Preapplication Meeting.3 Prior to the submittal of an application for a Special Use Permit, Zoning Text and/or Map Amendment (rezoning), or Conditional Zoning, or a Site Plan, a preapplication meeting must be held between the applicant and the Administrator, unless otherwise waived by the Administrator. During this meeting the applicant may submit a Concept Plan for preliminary review, comment, and recommendation by the Administrator. Section 3-1-2. Minimum Submission Standards. A. The Administrator shall establish minimum standards for submission requirements of all applications associated with the Zoning Ordinance. (1) Applications shall contain all information required to prove compliance with the minimum standards of the Ordinance, including, but not limited to: a. Written description of request and grounds for requesting; and b. Applicable district, use, and community design standards. B. Upon written request by an applicant, the Administrator may waive or modify a submission requirement(s) upon a determination that the information is not necessary to evaluate the merits of the application, such waivers or modiﬁcations are for application requirements only and do not include variances or modiﬁcations from Zoning District or Use Standards. C. Additional information may be required as deemed reasonably necessary by the Administrator. D. A fee shall be paid for the examination and approval or disapproval of every permit and application submitted. The fee shall be payable at the time of ﬁling to the Treasurer of Franklin County paid via the online permitting system in the amount required by a fee schedule adopted by the Board of Supervisors. Section 3-1-3. Online Forms. Applications for Subdivision Site Plans, Variances Appeals, Special Use Permits, Zoning Permits, Land Use Permits, or amendments to the Ordinance or Oﬃcial Zoning Map Amendment (rezoning) and any other request requiring action shall be made on forms provided by the County through the County's online permitting system. 1 Editor’s Note: This Article organizes all permit and application provisions in one place for improved referencing. 2 Editor’s Note: This Division is new and establishes general terms for the Article. 3 Editor’s Note: The County should consider if it wants to change this to require a preapplication meeting for Zoning Map Amendments, and for others to be optional. The planning commission decided to leave as drafted. Article 3 – Permits and Applications l Page 3-1 of 33 FRANKLIN COUNTY ZONING ORDINANCE UPDATE DRAFT ARTICLE 3 – PERMITS & APPLICATIONS l MARCH 26, 2026 Section 3-1-4. Ownership and Interests Disclosures. A. An applicant must disclose all equitable ownership of the real estate included in an application. In the case of corporate ownership, the name of stockholders, oﬃcers and directors shall be provided, and in any case the names and addresses of all of the real parties of interest in accordance with the Code of Virginia § 15.2-2289. B. Pursuant to the Code of Virginia § 15.2-2287 petitions brought by property owners, contract purchasers, or their agents, shall be sworn to under oath stating whether or not any member of the local Planning Commission or governing body has any interest in such property: (1) Either individually; (2) By ownership of stock in a corporation owning such land, partnership; (3) As the beneﬁciary of a trust; (4) As the settlor of a revocable trust; or (5) Whether a member of the immediate household or any member of the Planning Commission or governing body has any such interest. Sec. 25-789 Fee Schedule Section 3-1-5. Fees and Charges.4 A. The Board of Supervisors shall establish, by Ordinance, a schedule of fees, charges and expenses, and collection procedures for Zoning and Land Use Permits, Special Use Permits, variances, appeals, amendments, site plan reviews, and other matters pertaining to this Ordinance.5 B. The schedule of fees shall be available for inspection in the oﬃce of the Administrator and may be altered or amended by the Board of Supervisors by Ordinance amendment, as directed in Code of Virginia § 15.2-107. C. Delinquent Taxes and Charges.6 Pursuant to the Code of Virginia § 15.2-2286 (B), prior to the initiation of an application or appeal, the applicant and/or county shall produce satisfactory evidence that any delinquent real estate taxes, nuisance charges, stormwater management utility fees, and any other charges that constitute a lien on the subject property that are owed to the County, have been paid in full, unless otherwise authorized by the County Treasurer. (1) The above provision applies only to the property or properties for which the application is attached. (2) If an applicant is the renter of a subject property and said property has associated unpaid taxes and fees owed to the County, the property owner(s) shall be responsible for paying those balances in full. 4 Editor’s Note: This section replaces and expands upon existing Section 25-789. Editor’s Note: It is recommended that the County establish a fee schedule outside of the Zoning Ordinance in order to amend it when needed without necessitating amendment of this Ordinance. 6 Editor’s Note: The content in C. is new, per Code of VA. 5 Article 3 – Permits and Applications l Page 3-2 of 33 FRANKLIN COUNTY ZONING ORDINANCE UPDATE DRAFT ARTICLE 3 – PERMITS & APPLICATIONS l MARCH 26, 2026 Sec. 25-147 Utility-scale solar generation facility D. In situations where the Administrator anticipates expenses for professional services related to review of an application that will exceed the amount recouped by the imposition of standard fees, the County shall require the applicant to pay the cost of the professional review service.7 (1) Examples of projects for which a deposit may be warranted include (but are not limited to) rezoning requests, planned development districts, and Special Use Permits that require professional review Comprehensive Plan review. (2) The payment shall solely be applied to payment of professional services by engineers, attorneys, surveyors, architects, landscape architects, etc., that are speciﬁcally engaged by the County to consult directly on the applicant’s proposed project. (3) Payment is an express condition of the County’s determination upon the application. Payment does not guarantee approval of the application. Nor does payment create a client relationship between the applicant and the professional services provider. Section 3-1-6. Withdrawal of Applications. 8 Sec. 25-740 Withdrawal of petitions A. Any application ﬁled pursuant to Division 3-2 of this Article may be withdrawn upon written request by the applicant prior to the submission of any public hearing notice for advertisement; provided: (1) If the request for withdrawal is made after the notice of hearing is published, such withdrawal shall be only with the consent of whichever body has advertised the hearing; and (2) The same petition shall not be reconsidered within 12 months of the date of action, unless the respective body approving withdrawal speciﬁes that the time limitation shall not apply. Section 3-1-7. Reconsiderations. A. The following shall apply for all zoning text and map amendment; conditional zoning; special use permits; and variance applications: (1) If denied by the Board of Supervisors, then such application, or one substantially similar, shall not be reconsidered sooner than 12 months from the date of the previous denial. (2) If denied by the BZA, then such application, or one substantially similar, shall not be reconsidered sooner than 12 months after the previous denial. B. The limits on reconsideration shall not impair the right of either the Planning Commission or the Board of Supervisors to propose any amendment to this Ordinance on their motion at any time. DIVISION 3-2. ZONING TEXT AND MAP AMENDMENTS9 Section 3-2-1. In General. Pursuant to the Code of Virginia § 15.2-2286 (7) whenever public necessity, convenience, general welfare, or good zoning practice requires, the Board of Supervisors may, from time to time, amend, 7 Editor’s Note: Language from existing Section 25-147 is included here. Editor’s Note: From Section 25-740 of the existing ordinance. 9 Editor’s Note: This Division consolidates all zoning text and map amendment language in one place for ease of referencing. 8 Article 3 – Permits and Applications l Page 3-3 of 33 FRANKLIN COUNTY ZONING ORDINANCE UPDATE DRAFT ARTICLE 3 – PERMITS & APPLICATIONS l MARCH 26, 2026 supplement or change, by Ordinance, the boundaries of the Zoning Districts or the regulations established in this Ordinance. Section 3-2-2. Standards and Procedures. 10 A. Initiation of change. Pursuant to the Code of Virginia § 15.2-2286 (7) any amendment to this Ordinance or the Zoning Map may be initiated by:11 (1) Resolution of the Board of Supervisors. (2) Resolution of the Planning Commission; or (3) Application of the owner, contract purchaser with the owner’s written consent, or the owner’s agent, of the property proposed to be rezoned. a. The application shall be addressed to the Franklin County Board of Supervisors or Planning Commission, who shall forward such application to the Board of Supervisors. B. Zoning Map Amendments. Applications for Zoning Map Amendments, including Conditional Zoning requests, shall be made to the Administrator and accompanied by a Concept Plan as detailed in Division 6 Division 3-6 of this Article.12 (1) The Director of Planning and Zoning or designee will transmit the application and other information to any state, county, or other government agencies for review and comment, as appropriate. (2) After the application is determined to be complete, and all agency comments have been received, County staﬀ will provide comments in writing to the applicant so revisions can be made, if necessary the county will collect all comments from other agencies to be included in the staff report. The staff report will be emailed to the applicant(s) once the Planning Commission has received their packets. Any revisions can be made by applicant(s), if necessary. (3) The Director of Planning and Zoning or designee will prepare and submit a written staﬀ report to the Planning Commission on the proposed zoning map amendment. (4) A Site Plan is required as detailed in Division 6 Division 3-7 of this Article. C. Standards for review. (1) The application for a rezoning or Zoning Text Amendment shall be referred to the Planning Commission for public hearing and recommendation. The Planning Commission shall present their recommendation on the proposed ordinance or amendment, including the Zoning Map, to the Board of Supervisors for public hearing and action. No recommendation or action shall be rendered until public notiﬁcations and hearings have been conducted in accordance with Division 3-10 of this Article. 10 Editor’s Note: This section includes updated information from existing ordinance Section 25-732 and updated Code of Virginia references. 11 Editor’s Note: The current ordinance does not allow the Planning Commission to initiate a Zoning Map Amendment. BG recommends changing this as written in this section. Recommendation accepted. 12 Editor’s Note: The requirement for a concept plan has been applied to all zoning map amendments and consolidated in one place rather than stated in each of the planned districts and overlays sections. Article 3 – Permits and Applications l Page 3-4 of 33 FRANKLIN COUNTY ZONING ORDINANCE UPDATE DRAFT ARTICLE 3 – PERMITS & APPLICATIONS l MARCH 26, 2026 (2) The Planning Commission shall advise the Board of Supervisors of their recommendation within 100 days from its ﬁrst meeting following the referral of the application. If after 100 days no recommendation has been made, the governing body shall assume that the Planning Commission concurs with the applicant and supports the amendment. The Board of Supervisors shall thereafter take any action it deems appropriate, unless the applicant requests an extension for a deﬁned period not to exceed a total of 90 calendar days13 from the date of the public hearing. (3) All motions, resolutions, or applications for amendment to the Zoning Ordinance and/or Zoning Map shall be acted upon, and a decision made within such reasonable time as may be necessary which shall not exceed 12 months unless the applicant requests or consents to action beyond such period or unless the applicant withdraws his motion, resolution, or application for amendment to the Zoning Ordinance or map, or both; otherwise, the amendment shall be deemed approved. a. In the event of and upon a withdrawal by the applicant, processing of the motion, resolution, or petition shall cease without further action as otherwise would be required. Sec. 25-733 Proffers and conditions, Sec. 25-734 Effect of conditions D. All changes aﬀecting the Zoning Map that are approved by the Board of Supervisors shall be entered onto the oﬃcial Zoning Map within 60 days following the approval of such changes. DIVISION 3-3. CONDITIONAL ZONING AND PROFFERS14 Section 3-3-1. Purpose and Intent. 15 Conditional Zoning provides a method for permitting the reasonable and orderly development of land through Zoning Map Amendments with reasonable conditions governing the use and development of such property. As authorized under the Code of Virginia §§ 15.2-2296 through 15.2-2303.3, reasonable conditions may be voluntarily proﬀered for the protection of the community when combined with existing Zoning Ordinance district regulations. The exercise of authority shall not be construed to limit or restrict powers otherwise granted nor to aﬀect the validity of any Ordinance adopted by the locality which would be valid without regard to this Division. In addition, the provisions of this Division shall not be used for the purpose of discrimination in housing. Section 3-3-2. Standards and Procedures. 16 Sec. 25-735 Zoning map notation not included A. Proﬀers of conditions; standards of consideration. 13 Editor’s Note: 13 “calendar days” changed to “days” per Planning Commission worksession on Feb. 24, 2026. Editor’s Note: This Division greatly expands upon Sections 25-733 & 734 of the existing ordinance, brings it into compliance with, and updates references to Code of Virginia. 15 Editor’s Note: Purpose and intent has been added in compliance with Code of Virginia. 16 Editor’s Note: Section 25-735 Zoning map notation (existing ordinance) was not included. Any such proﬀered conditions must: a. Be in accordance with the procedures and standards contained in the Code of Virginia §§ 15.2-2297 and 15.2-2298; and b. Be submitted by the following deadlines:17 i. Proposed proﬀered conditions, regardless of whether they are signed by the owners of all parcels subject to the Zoning Map Amendment, shall be submitted to the Administrator by 6:00 p.m. on the day before the day of the Commission's scheduled public hearing on the Zoning Map Amendment. ii. Proposed proﬀered conditions, signed by the owners of all parcels subject to the Zoning Map Amendment, shall be submitted to the Administrator by 6:00 5:00 p.m. on the day of the Council's Board of Supervisors' scheduled public hearing on the Zoning Map Amendment. (2) Proﬀered conditions shall be subject to the following limitations: a. The rezoning itself must give rise to the need for the conditions. b. The conditions shall have a reasonable relation to the rezoning. c. The conditions shall not include a cash contribution to the County. d. The conditions shall not include mandatory dedication of real or personal property for open space, parks, schools, ﬁre departments, or other public facilities not otherwise provided for in the Zoning Ordinance of the County of Franklin. e. The conditions shall not include a requirement that the applicant create a property owners’ association under the Property Owners’ Association Act (§ 55.1-1800 et seq.) that includes an express further condition that members of a property owners’ association pay an assessment for the maintenance of public facilities owned in fee by a public entity, including open space, parks, schools, ﬁre departments, and other public facilities not otherwise provided for in the Code of Virginia § 15.2-2241; however, such facilities shall not include sidewalks, special street signs or markers, or special street lighting in public rights-of-way not maintained by the Virginia Department of Transportation. f. The conditions must not include payment for, or construction of, oﬀ-site improvements except those provided for in the Code of Virginia §§ 15.2-2241 and 15.2-2303.4. g. All conditions shall be related to the physical development or physical operation of the property. h. The conditions shall be in accordance with the Franklin County Comprehensive Plan. 17 Editor’s Note: Per Franklin County staﬀ review (March 2025), provision revised to reﬂect the current practice. No agent of the County has suggested or demanded a proﬀered condition that is unreasonable under applicable law.” b. “I hereby proﬀer that the development of the subject property of this application shall be in strict accordance with the conditions proffers set forth in this submission.” (4) Each application for rezoning which proposes proﬀered conditions to be applied to the property shall be accompanied by the following items beyond those required by conventional rezoning requests: a. The Agricultural District covers the largest portion of the County which is presently occupied by farms, forests, conservation areas and other types of rural uses. It is designed to protect these existing conditions and to encourage only that future development which promotes the preservation of the rural qualities of the County. In addition, selected business and industrial uses may be permitted in the district but only when the governing body finds that such development not only enables the rural characteristics of the County to be maintained but is in harmony with the economic development objectives of the County. Article 19 of the Zoning Ordinance was established to provide general guidelines for the citing of telecommunication towers and antennas. The goals of this article are to: (i) encourage the location of towers in nonresidential areas and minimize the total number of towers and tower sites throughout the community; (ii) encourage utilization of publicly held lands; (iii) encourage strongly the joint use of new and existing tower sites; (iv) encourage users of towers and antennas to locate them, to the extent possible, in areas where the adverse impact on the community is minimal; (v) encourage users of towers and antennas to configure them in a way that minimizes the adverse visual impact of the towers and antennas; and (vi) provide adequate sites for the provision of telecommunication services with minimal negative impact on the resources of the county. Avoid during public meetings and during the performance of public duties the-use of abusive, threatening or intimidating language or gestures directed at colleagues, citizens, or personnel. 2. Pay all taxes due to the County, state, or national government. 3. Avoid a private lifestyle that casts public doubt upon the integrity and competence of the County government. 4. Make a conscientious effort to be well prepared for each meeting. 5. Recognizing the dignity of each individual , the Board shall attempt to avoid offering public criticism of colleagues or County employees. 6. Work to create a positive environment in public meeting where citizens will feel comfortable in their roles as observers or participants . 7. Maintain an attitude of courtesy and consideration toward all colleagues and staff during all discussions and deliberations. 8. Be tolerant. Allow citizens, employees, or colleagues sufficient opportunity to present their views. 9. Be respectful and attentive. Avoid comments, body language or distracting activity that conveys a message of disrespect for the presentations from citizens, personnel, or colleagues . Be concise. 10. Avoid the practice of taking more time to address an issue before the body than is necessary and essential for an adequate consideration of those matters being discussed . Board members should always remember, "There is no right way to do the wrong thing ." HALIFAX COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS CONDUCT OF THE PUBLIC The efficient and dignified conduct of public business is an ultimate concern of the Board. Accordingly, it is the policy of the Board that its meetings be conducted with the highest degree of order and decorum . The Board's integrity and dignity will be established and maintained at all times during the conduct of public business, and the Board will permit no behavior which is not in keeping with this policy. Prohibited conduct at meetings shall include: 1. 2. 3. Campaigning for public office, soliciting of funds, or promoting private business ventures . Using profanity, vulgar language or gestures. Language or actions which insult or demean any person or group of persons or which , when directed at a public official or employee is not related to his official duties. 4. Disruptive behavior. 5. Making non-germane or frivolous statements. 6. Discussions of a sectarian or partisan nature. 7. Smoking or eating in the Board Room. 8. Addressing question or statements to anyone other than the Chairman (Questions shall be presented to the Chairman , who will, at their discretion, solicit a response from the appropriate board or staff member.) 9. Standing in the back or side isles of the Board Room as long as there are sufficient seats available (except for law enforcement personnel). 10. Persons in attendance at the meeting addressing the Board while members of the Board are considering any motion , resolution or ordinance preliminary to a vote on the same, except at the discretion of the Chairman. 11. Any persons addressing comments or questions to someone other than the Chairman. 12. Wearing hats, caps or other types of headgear. 13. Applause is permitted only during presentations, awards, proclamations and special recognition periods. The Board of Supervisors welcomes and encourages citizen participation in its meetings. To insure fair and timely participation, the following procedures are observed by the Board : 1. 2. All presenters are asked to state their name Each speaker on a general matter, whether an individual or a representative for an organization , is limited to three (3) minutes. 3. Speaker's comments are limited to a presentation on his or her point of view only - questions of clarification may be entertained only by the board members; 4. All comments are to be directed to the board; 5. Debate between a recognized speaker and audience members or between board members and the speaker is not permitted; 6. Courtesy between the speaker and audience is expected at all times ; 7. Speakers are requested to leave any written statement and/ or comments with the clerk to the board ; 8. Individuals speaking on behalf of an organized group are required to file with the clerk written authorization from the group allowing the individual to represent that group; 9. By applying to speak as a representative for an organization , the individual confirms they are recognized as an official representative of that organization ; and 10. Presentation to the board by groups should: a. Obtain prior approval from the chairman of the board; • b. Submit all written materials and data no later than ten days prior to the meeting in time to be included in the board's agenda packet distributed a week before each regular monthly meeting; c. Limit presentations to fifteen minutes; and d. File with the clerk written authorization from the group allowing the individual to represent that group. 11 . A digital, color-coded timer will be displayed in full view of the Board, the speaker, and individuals seated in the gallery. When two minutes have expired, the timer display will turn yellow indicating the speaker has one minute to conclude his/her comments. At the end of that one-minute period (completion of the full three-minute period), the timer will display 0:00 in red , indicating the speaker must relinquish the podium to the next speaker. Staff will notify the Chairman that the speaker's time has expired . Speakers continuing after the time allotted shall be ruled out of order by the Chairman. The Chairman shall preserve order and decorum at all meetings. The Chairman may order the expulsion of any person for violation of these rules, disruptive behavior, or any words or action which incite violence or disorder, subject to appeal to the Board . Any person so expelled shall not be readmitted for the remainder of the meeting from which he was expelled. Any person who has been so expelled and who at a later meeting again engages in words or actions justifying expulsion may be barred from attendance at future meetings of the Board for a specified and reasonable period of time not to exceed six months or upon a still subsequent expulsion , a period not to exceed one year either by the Chairman , subject to appeal to the Board , or by motion passed by the Board . PUBLIC HEARINGS P6 ALIF OUNTY Staff Report Staff Members: Meeting Date: October 20, 2026 Detrick Easley Item# D-1 Ordinance# 2026-44 Department: Planning & Zoning Subject: Solar Ordinance Revisions Background: As of April 2026, Virginia energy legislation is expanding renewable energy development while defining the role .and authority oflocal governments through the passage of Senate Bills 347. This bill establishes a standardized regulatory framework that limits local discretion and approval of solar facilities. Senate Bill 347 requires that ground-mounted solar energy generation facilities of 1 MW or greater be reviewed through a special exception (or use permit) process unless they are permitted by right. This applies to zoning districts classified as agricultural, commercial, industrial, or institutional. If allowing by special exception or use permit, localities should update their zoning ordinances to include provisions addressing setbacks, fencing, panel height, screening, visual impacts, grading, and decommissioning plans as limited by the provisions of the new law. Procedurally, SB347 also require localities to report their special exception decisions to the State Corporation Commission (SCC), including reasons for denial, consistency with the Comprehensive Plan, and the date of the most recent plan update. This does contemplate that, while a local Planning Commission may determine that a project is not in accord with the comprehensive plan for the purposes of review under 15.2-2232 of the Code of Virginia, the application should be further and finally acted upon by the local governing body. P7 The purpose of this public hearing is to receive public comments regarding proposed amendments to the Halifax County Solar Energy Facilities Ordinance. The proposed amendments have been prepared in response to recent changes in Virginia law governing the development and local regulation of solar energy facilities. The County's objective is to update its existing regulations, establish consistency between the Zoning Ordinance and Comprehensive Plan, and provide clear guidance for future solar energy development while exercising the land-use authority available to the County under state law. Halifax County has experienced significant interest in utility-scale solar energy development over the past several years. As additional projects have been proposed, the County has evaluated the potential effects of solar development on agricultural and forestal lands, adjoining properties, transportation infrastructure, environmental resources, and the long-term use of land. The County previously established regulations addressing the location, construction, operation, and decommissioning of solar energy facilities. However, recent changes in Virginia law require the County to reevaluate portions of its existing ordinance to determine whether local requirements remain consistent with state regulations. The County engaged the Berkeley Group to assist with reviewing and preparing proposed amendments to the Solar Energy Facilities Ordinance and Comprehensive Plan. The proposed amendments address the County's regulatory approach to solar energy facilities, including the following subjects: The revisions are intended to bring local solar regulations into alignment with applicable Virginia law and clarify the County's authority in reviewing solar development applications. Avoid during public meetings and during the performance of public duties the-use of abusive, threatening or intimidating language or gestures directed at colleagues, citizens, or personnel. 2. Pay all taxes due to the County, state, or national government. 3. Avoid a private lifestyle that casts public doubt upon the integrity and competence of the County government. 4. Make a conscientious effort to be well prepared for each meeting. 5. Recognizing the dignity of each individual , the Board shall attempt to avoid offering public criticism of colleagues or County employees. 6. Work to create a positive environment in public meeting where citizens will feel comfortable in their roles as observers or participants . 7. Maintain an attitude of courtesy and consideration toward all colleagues and staff during all discussions and deliberations. 8. Be tolerant. Allow citizens, employees, or colleagues sufficient opportunity to present their views. 9. Be respectful and attentive. Avoid comments, body language or distracting activity that conveys a message of disrespect for the presentations from citizens, personnel, or colleagues . Be concise. 10. Avoid the practice of taking more time to address an issue before the body than is necessary and essential for an adequate consideration of those matters being discussed . Board members should always remember, "There is no right way to do the wrong thing ." HALIFAX COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS CONDUCT OF THE PUBLIC The efficient and dignified conduct of public business is an ultimate concern of the Board. Accordingly, it is the policy of the Board that its meetings be conducted with the highest degree of order and decorum . The Board's integrity and dignity will be established and maintained at all times during the conduct of public business, and the Board will permit no behavior which is not in keeping with this policy. Prohibited conduct at meetings shall include: 1. 2. 3. Campaigning for public office, soliciting of funds, or promoting private business ventures . Using profanity, vulgar language or gestures. Language or actions which insult or demean any person or group of persons or which , when directed at a public official or employee is not related to his official duties. 4. Disruptive behavior. 5. Making non-germane or frivolous statements. 6. Discussions of a sectarian or partisan nature. 7. Smoking or eating in the Board Room. 8. Addressing question or statements to anyone other than the Chairman (Questions shall be presented to the Chairman , who will, at their discretion, solicit a response from the appropriate board or staff member.) 9. Standing in the back or side isles of the Board Room as long as there are sufficient seats available (except for law enforcement personnel). 10. Persons in attendance at the meeting addressing the Board while members of the Board are considering any motion , resolution or ordinance preliminary to a vote on the same, except at the discretion of the Chairman. 11. Any persons addressing comments or questions to someone other than the Chairman. 12. Wearing hats, caps or other types of headgear. 13. Applause is permitted only during presentations, awards, proclamations and special recognition periods. The Board of Supervisors welcomes and encourages citizen participation in its meetings. To insure fair and timely participation, the following procedures are observed by the Board : 1. 2. All presenters are asked to state their name Each speaker on a general matter, whether an individual or a representative for an organization , is limited to three (3) minutes. 3. Speaker's comments are limited to a presentation on his or her point of view only - questions of clarification may be entertained only by the board members; 4. All comments are to be directed to the board; 5. Debate between a recognized speaker and audience members or between board members and the speaker is not permitted; 6. Courtesy between the speaker and audience is expected at all times ; 7. Speakers are requested to leave any written statement and/ or comments with the clerk to the board ; 8. Individuals speaking on behalf of an organized group are required to file with the clerk written authorization from the group allowing the individual to represent that group; 9. By applying to speak as a representative for an organization , the individual confirms they are recognized as an official representative of that organization ; and 10. Presentation to the board by groups should: a. Obtain prior approval from the chairman of the board; • b. Submit all written materials and data no later than ten days prior to the meeting in time to be included in the board's agenda packet distributed a week before each regular monthly meeting; c. Limit presentations to fifteen minutes; and d. File with the clerk written authorization from the group allowing the individual to represent that group. 11 . A digital, color-coded timer will be displayed in full view of the Board, the speaker, and individuals seated in the gallery. When two minutes have expired, the timer display will turn yellow indicating the speaker has one minute to conclude his/her comments. At the end of that one-minute period (completion of the full three-minute period), the timer will display 0:00 in red , indicating the speaker must relinquish the podium to the next speaker. Staff will notify the Chairman that the speaker's time has expired . Speakers continuing after the time allotted shall be ruled out of order by the Chairman. The Chairman shall preserve order and decorum at all meetings. The Chairman may order the expulsion of any person for violation of these rules, disruptive behavior, or any words or action which incite violence or disorder, subject to appeal to the Board . Any person so expelled shall not be readmitted for the remainder of the meeting from which he was expelled. Any person who has been so expelled and who at a later meeting again engages in words or actions justifying expulsion may be barred from attendance at future meetings of the Board for a specified and reasonable period of time not to exceed six months or upon a still subsequent expulsion , a period not to exceed one year either by the Chairman , subject to appeal to the Board , or by motion passed by the Board . PUBLIC HEARINGS P6 ALIF OUNTY Staff Report Staff Members: Meeting Date: October 20, 2026 Detrick Easley Item# D-1 Ordinance# 2026-44 Department: Planning & Zoning Subject: Solar Ordinance Revisions Background: As of April 2026, Virginia energy legislation is expanding renewable energy development while defining the role .and authority oflocal governments through the passage of Senate Bills 347. This bill establishes a standardized regulatory framework that limits local discretion and approval of solar facilities. Senate Bill 347 requires that ground-mounted solar energy generation facilities of 1 MW or greater be reviewed through a special exception (or use permit) process unless they are permitted by right. This applies to zoning districts classified as agricultural, commercial, industrial, or institutional. If allowing by special exception or use permit, localities should update their zoning ordinances to include provisions addressing setbacks, fencing, panel height, screening, visual impacts, grading, and decommissioning plans as limited by the provisions of the new law. Procedurally, SB347 also require localities to report their special exception decisions to the State Corporation Commission (SCC), including reasons for denial, consistency with the Comprehensive Plan, and the date of the most recent plan update. This does contemplate that, while a local Planning Commission may determine that a project is not in accord with the comprehensive plan for the purposes of review under 15.2-2232 of the Code of Virginia, the application should be further and finally acted upon by the local governing body. P7 The purpose of this public hearing is to receive public comments regarding proposed amendments to the Halifax County Solar Energy Facilities Ordinance. The proposed amendments have been prepared in response to recent changes in Virginia law governing the development and local regulation of solar energy facilities. The County's objective is to update its existing regulations, establish consistency between the Zoning Ordinance and Comprehensive Plan, and provide clear guidance for future solar energy development while exercising the land-use authority available to the County under state law. Halifax County has experienced significant interest in utility-scale solar energy development over the past several years. As additional projects have been proposed, the County has evaluated the potential effects of solar development on agricultural and forestal lands, adjoining properties, transportation infrastructure, environmental resources, and the long-term use of land. The County previously established regulations addressing the location, construction, operation, and decommissioning of solar energy facilities. However, recent changes in Virginia law require the County to reevaluate portions of its existing ordinance to determine whether local requirements remain consistent with state regulations. The County engaged the Berkeley Group to assist with reviewing and preparing proposed amendments to the Solar Energy Facilities Ordinance and Comprehensive Plan. The proposed amendments address the County's regulatory approach to solar energy facilities, including the following subjects: The revisions are intended to bring local solar regulations into alignment with applicable Virginia law and clarify the County's authority in reviewing solar development applications. Adjournment Hanover County Planning Commission Public Hearing Rules The purpose of public hearings is to allow the public an opportunity to speak to the Commission on matters within its purview, including rezoning and conditional use permit requests, zoning and subdivision ordinance amendments, and comprehensive plan amendments. Comments made by speakers must relate to the matter being discussed, and all comments must be directed to the Commission. Questions posed by speakers will generally be answered at the end of the hearing by either the Commission or staff. During the public hearing, members of the Commission may ask questions of speakers to clarify comments or obtain other relevant information. The Commission may also ask any speaker questions for clarification after the public hearing has been closed. The procedure for a public hearing is as follows: 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. 8. 9. Planning Department staff will give a presentation outlining the request and staff’s recommendations. The applicant and/or his representative will have up to fifteen (15) minutes to make their presentation. The applicant or representative of the applicant may reserve up to five (5) minutes of the time allotted for its presentation for use as rebuttal time. After the applicant’s presentation, other proponents will have up to fifteen (15) minutes to speak, for a maximum of five (5) minutes each. Thereafter, opponents of the application will also have up to fifteen (15) minutes to speak, for a maximum of five (5) minutes each. Time consumed by the Commission asking questions and a speaker’s responses will not count against these limits. Proponents and opponents may not yield their allotted time to other speakers. If the Chairman determines that the issues involved are unusually complex, or that a large number of persons desire to speak, these time limits may be adjusted, provided that the amount of time will be allotted equally to proponents and opponents. After the applicant, proponents, and opponents have spoken, the Chairman will declare the public hearing closed and the Commission will then deliberate and vote on the application. No public hearing may extend beyond two (2) hours unless approved by majority vote of the Commission. All speakers and others in the meeting room must maintain proper decorum and demonstrate civility toward the Commission, staff, applicants, and the public at large. The Chairman shall be responsible for enforcing the rules of the Planning Commission, including those related to decorum and civility. All Planning Commission meetings are streamed live. To access the live stream, visit our website at www.hanovercounty.gov. Hanover: People, Tradition and Spirit

The County has conducted examinations of title to the property and has not been able to make a bona fide offer to purchase the Easements because the Owner is deceased and the heir is unwilling to sign. This Board paper authorizes the County Attorney to institute and conduct condemnation proceedings in accordance with the Code of Virginia. This Board paper further authorizes and directs the County Manager to continue to seek a voluntary acquisition of the easements, to take all steps necessary to acquire the easements, and to enter on and take possession of the required easements in accordance with the Code of Virginia. The Directors of Public Works and Real Property recommend approval of this Board paper; the County Manager concurs. Resolution - Condemnation - Easements - Mount Olive Avenue Realignment Project - 8820 Mount Olive Avenue - Fairfield District. This Board paper authorizes condemnation proceedings for property that is needed for the construction of the Mount Olive Avenue Realignment project. The County needs to acquire 933 square feet of permanent utility easement, 416 square feet of permanent sight distance easement, and 110 square feet of temporary entrance easement across the property located at 8820 Mount Olive Avenue, identified as Tax Map Parcel 782-760-2632, and owned by Barbara C. Anderson and Charles F. Anderson. Based on an independent appraisal, the County made an offer of $5,410 for the required property interests, but the parties have not reached an agreement. This Board paper authorizes the County Attorney to institute and conduct condemnation proceedings in accordance with the Code of Virginia. This Board paper further authorizes and directs the County Manager to continue to seek a voluntary acquisition of the easements, to take all steps necessary to acquire the easements, and to enter on and take possession of the required easements in accordance with the Code of Virginia. The Directors of Public Works and Real Property recommend approval of this Board paper; the County Manager concurs. 4 Resolution - Signatory Authority - Lease to BP Seafood LLC - 3408 Old Parham Road Three Chopt District. This Board paper authorizes the County Manager to execute a lease with BP Seafood LLC and Bruce and April Givens for their operation of a seafood market at 3408 Old Parham Road. The County acquired this property, which is near the intersection of West Broad Street and North Parham Road, for a future transit project. At the time of the County’s acquisition, the County assumed a preexisting lease with BP Seafood LLC and the Givenses. That assumed lease will expire on October 31, 2026. The County has no immediate need of the property, and the tenants wish to continue operating their seafood market at the current location. The initial term of the new lease would be one year, beginning on November 1, 2026, and monthly rent would be $3,713.82. The parties would have the option to renew the lease for up to three additional one-year terms, and during any such renewal term, monthly rent would increase by $100 from the previous term. The Directors of Public Works and Real Property recommend approval of this Board paper; the County Manager concurs. Public Comment General Agenda Resolution - Award of Contract - Western Government Center Elevator Modernization - Brookland District. This Board paper awards a fixed-price contract for $1,267,000 to Virtexco Corporation for the Western Government Center Elevator Modernization project. The project consists of modernizing four elevators in the Courthouse and Jail West

This Board paper authorizes condemnation proceedings for property that is needed for the construction of the Fall Line Trail Longdale Phase project. The County needs to acquire permanent joint use utility easements containing 4,011 square feet across the properties located at 1501 and 1519 Mountain Road and owned by Ridge Homes, LLC. Based on independent appraisals, the County made an offer of $6,607 for the required property interests, but the parties have not reached an agreement. This Board paper authorizes the County Attorney to institute and conduct condemnation proceedings in accordance with the Code of Virginia. This Board paper further authorizes and directs the County Manager to continue to seek a voluntary acquisition of the easements, to take all steps necessary to acquire the easements, and to enter on and take possession of the required easements in accordance with the Code of Virginia. The Directors of Public Works and Real Property recommend approval of this Board paper; the County Manager concurs. Public Comment General Agenda Introduction of Ordinance - To Add Article XIV, Titled “Marijuana Sales Tax,” to Chapter 20 of the Code of the County of Henrico to Tax the Sale of Marijuana and Marijuana Products at a Rate of Three and One-Half Percent in Accordance with State Law. This Board paper introduces for advertisement and a public hearing on November 10, 2026, proposed ordinance amendments to levy a local marijuana sales tax at the rate of three and one-half percent on any sale of any marijuana or marijuana products in accordance with state law. State law currently requires the rate to remain in effect for at least three years. The Finance Director recommends approval of this Board paper, and the County Manager concurs. Introduction of Ordinance - To Amend and Reordain Section 13-27 Titled “Reserved” of the Code of the County of Henrico to Prohibit Consuming Marijuana or Marijuana Products, or Offering to Another, in Certain Public Places; Prohibit Consuming or Possessing Marijuana or Marijuana Products in or on Public School Grounds; and Regulate the Time of Sale of Marijuana or Marijuana Products. This Board paper introduces for advertisement and a public hearing on November 10, 2026, proposed ordinance amendments to prohibit consuming marijuana or marijuana products, or offering marijuana or marijuana products to others, in public parks, playgrounds, public streets, or any sidewalk adjoining any public street. The amendments also prohibit consuming or possessing marijuana or marijuana products in or on public school grounds. Finally, the amendments establish hours during which marijuana and marijuana products may be sold by retail marijuana stores and microbusinesses licensed by the Virginia Cannabis Control Authority. The Chief of Police recommends approval of this Board paper, and the County Manager concurs. Resolution - Signatory Authority - Memorandum of Understanding with Housing Families First for a Housing Coaching and Counseling Pilot Program. This Board paper authorizes the County Manager to execute and administer a memorandum of understanding with Housing Families First (“HFF”) in a form approved by the County Attorney. It also authorizes the County Manager to execute any future amendments necessary to administer or extend the pilot program in a form approved by the County Attorney. The memorandum of understanding provides for donations to HFF for the purpose of funding a full-time staff position providing housing coaching and counseling programming to current residents of Glenwood Farms, with the goal of ensuring that current residents can continue to live in the community as it is transformed into a modern mixed-income community with a variety of housing types. The initial donation for the pilot program is $66,000. The Director of Community Revitalization recommends approval of the Board paper, and the County Manager concurs. Resolution - Signatory Authority - Amended and Restated Memorandum of Understanding - Maggie Walker Community Land Trust - Varina District. This Board paper authorizes the County Manager to execute an amended and restated memorandum of understanding with the Maggie Walker Community Land Trust. The Trust proposes to acquire 20 already constructed single-family homes within the Arcadia development. Under the community land trust model, these homes will be available to qualified purchasers earning no more than 115% of the area median income for the Richmond metropolitan area. The Board of Supervisors will make a grant of $500,00 to the Trust to 2 support the affordability of the homes, and the Trust will solicit at least $300,000 in matching donations. The Director of Community Revitalization recommends approval of this Board paper, and the County Manager concurs. Resolution - Award of Contract - Fall Line Trail Southern Sections - Fairfield District. This Board paper would award a unit price contract of $15,918,413.45 to Crowder Construction Company for the Fall Line Trail – Southern Sections project. The project package includes four Fall Line Trail projects: Lakeside Community Trail Phase 2, Lakeside Community Trail Phase 3, Brook Road and Hilliard Road Trail, and the Hilliard Road Safety and Mobility Improvements. The project consists of the construction of a shared use path approximately 1.6 miles long and 12-feet wide extending from the intersection of Dumbarton Road and Gillespie Avenue to the intersection of Brook Road and Lakeside Avenue, approximately 0.5 mile of bike lanes on Hilliard Road from Lakeside Avenue to the Fall Line Trail crossing, pedestrian bridges and boardwalks, a pedestrian hybrid beacon on Dumbarton Road, an overhead rectangular rapid flashing beacon on Hilliard Road, ADA compliant ramps within the project limits, and new storm sewer and stormwater management facilities. Work on the project is anticipated to begin in November 2026 and be completed within 730 calendar days. The County received two bids on August 18, 2026, in response to ITB 26-2970-5JL and Addendum No. 1 for construction of the Fall Line Trail – Southern Sections project, and the bids were as follows: Bidders Crowder Construction Company Charlotte, NC Sagres Construction Corporation Spotsylvania, VA Bid Amounts $15,918,413.45 $23,426,265.25 Based upon a review of the bids, Crowder Construction Company is the lowest responsive and responsible bidder. The final contract amount will be determined upon completion of the project by multiplying the unit quantities authorized by the County by the unit prices submitted in the contractor’s bid. Funding to support the contract is available within the project budget. The Directors of Public Works and Purchasing recommend approval of the Board paper, and the County Manager concurs. Resolution - Award of Contract - Three Chopt Road Improvements - Three Chopt and Tuckahoe Districts. This Board paper awards a unit price contract of $45,531,364 to Shirley Contracting Company, LLC for the Three Chopt Road Improvements project. The project package includes improvements to Three Chopt Road beginning at the intersection with Barrington Hill Drive and ending at a point approximately 1,000 feet east of Gaskins Road, including four-lane curb and 3 gutter roadway with either a flush shared center left turn lane or a raised median, four-foot sidewalks on both sides of the roadway, and enclosed drainage, public water, sanitary sewer, signage, and pavement markings. Work on the project is anticipated to begin in November 2026 and be completed within 1,096 calendar days. The County received three bids on September 1, 2026, in response to ITB 26-2963-5JL and Addenda Nos. 1, 2, and 3. The bids were as follows: Bidders Bid Amounts Shirley Contracting Company, LLC $45,531,364.00 Lorton, VA Branch Civil, Inc. $48,935,850.00 Roanoke, VA Sagres Construction Corporation $51,470,999.99 Alexandria, VA Based upon a review of the bids, Shirley Contracting Company, LLC is the lowest responsive and responsible bidder. The final contract amount will be determined upon completion of the project by multiplying the unit quantities authorized by the County by the unit prices submitted in the contractor’s bid. Funding to support the contract is available within the project budget. The Directors of Public Works and Purchasing recommend approval of the Board paper, and the County Manager concurs. 4

HENRY COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS MINUTES September 22, 2026 – 3:00 p.m. The Henry County Board of Supervisors held its regular meeting on September 22, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. in the Summerlin Meeting Room of the County Administration Building, 3300 Kings Mountain Road, Collinsville, Virginia. The following Board members were present: Jim Adams, Chairman; Travis Pruitt, Vice Chairman; Chris Lawless; Debra Buchanan; Garrett Dillard; and Pam Cobler. Staff members present were Dale Wagoner, County Administrator; JR Powell, Deputy County Administrator; George Lyle, County Attorney; Crystal Ferguson, Deputy Director of Finance; Michelle Via, Director of Human Resources; Brandon Martin, Public Information Officer; and Jennifer Gregory, Executive Assistant. Sheriff Wayne Davis, Lt. Colonel Eric Hairston, Major Danny Harold, Captain Sandy Hines, and Sgt. Tim Robertson of the Sheriff's Office were present. Bill Wyatt of the Martinsville Bulletin, Taylor Boyd of the Henry County Enterprise, and Charles Roark of Star News were also present. INVOCATION AND PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Chairman Adams gave the invocation, and Ms. Buchanan led the Pledge of Allegiance. CALL TO ORDER: Chairman Adams called the meeting to order and welcomed everyone. He stated that anyone wishing to be on the agenda for the Board's regular business meeting at 3:00 p.m. must contact the County Administrator's Office at least 7 days before the meeting. Those wishing to speak at the Board's public meeting starting at 6:00 p.m. may do so under the agenda item - Matters Presented by the Public, without contacting the County Administrator's Office. ITEMS OF CONSENT: Confirmation of Minutes of Meetings Copy included in Board's File.  August 25, 2026 (Regular Meeting) Summary of Accounts Payable Copy included in Board's File.  September 22, 2026 MONTHLY REPORT ON DELINQUENT TAX COLLECTION EFFORTS Tiffanie S. Hairston, Treasurer, noted that 95.22% of 2025 real estate taxes and 90.29% of 2025 personal property taxes had been collected. Since January 1, 2026, TACS has collected approximately $894,144.35. In addition, TACS collected 557 Vehicle Registration Withholding (VRW) stops in July 2026 and 411 in August 2026. MONTHLY UPDATE FROM THE MARTINSVILLE-HENRY COUNTY ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION Mr. Mark Heath, President/CEO of the Martinsville-Henry County Economic Development Corporation, was present to give the monthly update to the Board. Mr. Heath reviewed a summary of activities by division (a Copy is included in the Board’s File). CONSIDERATION OF A RESOLUTION REGARDING COLONIAL DOWNS GROUP, LLC Dale Wagoner, County Administrator, said in 2004, Henry County voters approved a referendum allowing pari-mutuel wagering and off-track betting facilities in the County. Since 2021, Colonial Downs Group, LLC has operated a historical horse racing facility at 2360 Virginia Avenue in Collinsville. Colonial Downs Group, LLC has expressed interest in relocating its existing historical horse racing facility to a new location within Henry County. The proposed relocation would include new private investment and is expected to generate construction activity, permanent jobs, and additional economic benefits. The company has requested that the Board support the relocation, development, and operation of the proposed pari-mutuel wagering facility. Staff has prepared a resolution of support for the Board’s consideration (Copy included in Board’s File). On a motion by Mr. Pruitt and seconded by Mr. Lawless, the Board approved the resolution as presented by the following vote: AYES: Adams, Buchanan, Dillard, Lawless, and Pruitt. NAYS: Cobler. AWARD OF CONTRACT RE: REPLACEMENT VEHICLE – SHERIFF’S OFFICE Dale Wagoner, County Administrator, said Sheriff Wayne Davis is asking the Board to award a contract for $51,214 to Haley Ford in North Chesterfield, Virginia, to purchase a 2027 Ford F-250 XL 4x4 Truck for the Animal Services Division. Sheriff Davis has stated this vehicle will replace an existing vehicle with high mileage from the Animal Services Division. Pricing for the vehicle is based on the Virginia Sheriff’s Association vehicle procurement program and specifications. Funding for the replacement vehicles is included in the FY 2027 budget. On a motion by Mr. Pruitt and seconded by Mr. Lawless, the Board awarded a contract of $51,214 to Haley Ford to purchase the replacement vehicle for the Sheriff’s Department as presented by the following vote: AYES: Adams, Buchanan, Cobler, Dillard, Lawless, and Pruitt. NAYS: None. AWARD OF CONTRACT RE: VEHICLE EMERGENCY EQUIPMENT – SHERIFF’S OFFICE Dale Wagoner, County Administrator, said Sheriff Wayne Davis is asking the Board to award a contract for $71,864 to East Coast Emergency Vehicles, LLC in Chester, Virginia, to purchase emergency equipment for seven police vehicles. Sheriff Davis has stated that East Coast Emergency Vehicles, LLC, is the sole source supplier of this equipment, and this purchase has been approved by the Purchasing Department as such. Funding for this purchase is included in the FY 2027 budget. On a motion by Dr. Cobler and seconded by Ms. Buchanan, the Board awarded a contract for the emergency equipment as presented by the following vote: AYES: Adams, Buchanan, Cobler, Dillard, Lawless, and Pruitt. NAYS: None. AWARD OF CONTRACT RE: ASPHALT MAINTENANCE – BUILDINGS AND GROUNDS Dale Wagoner, County Administrator, said staff is asking the Board of Supervisors to award a contract of $64,800 to Commercial Parking Lot Services located in Blairs, Virginia, to repair and seal all asphalt surfaces for the Henry County complex, including the administration building, sheriff’s office, and courthouse areas. The Purchasing Department has reviewed and approved the contract for your consideration. Funding for this project is included in the FY 2026-27 capital budget. On a motion by Ms. Buchanan and seconded by Mr. Pruitt, the Board awarded a contract of $64,800 to Commercial Parking Lot Services for asphalt maintenance as presented by the following vote: AYES: Adams, Buchanan, Cobler, Dillard, Lawless, and Pruitt. NAYS: None. ADDITIONAL APPROPRIATION RE: SELF INSURANCE FUND – FINANCE DEPARTMENT Dale Wagoner, County Administrator, said in FY 2015, Henry County, the Henry County Public Service Authority, and Henry County Public Schools established a joint selfinsurance program to better manage employee health insurance costs and provide greater long-term stability for the participating organizations and their employees. The program has performed well over that period, allowing the participating organizations to maintain relatively modest rate increases while accumulating reserves to help manage fluctuations in claims. The Self-Insurance Fund balance peaked at approximately $9.5 million at the end of FY 2024. Following two years of increased claims and operating costs, the fund balance stood at approximately $6.9 million at the end of FY 2026 and, based on current projections, is expected to decline to approximately $4.5 million by the end of FY 2027. FY 2026, however, was an unusually difficult claims year. Medical and prescription claims exceeded budget revenues and contributions, resulting in an operating deficit. An appropriation of $1,750,000 from the Self-Insurance Fund balance is required to cover the FY 2026 shortfall. This experience is consistent with broader healthcare cost pressures. Nationally, employer health benefit costs were projected to increase approximately 6.7% in 2026, driven by increased utilization, high-cost claims, prescription drugs, and rising medical costs. Similar pressures are being experienced by the Commonwealth of Virginia, which provided for a 12.96% increase in state employee health insurance premiums for FY 2027 and additional funding to replenish its health insurance fund. The Self-Insurance Fund is intended, in part, to provide financial protection during unusually high claims years. However, the FY 2027 contribution rate was increased by only 3%, below the approximately 6% or greater increase recommended based on claims experience and projected healthcare costs. As a result, additional use of Self-Insurance Fund reserves may be necessary during FY 2027 if current trends continue. Adequate rate setting also affects retirees and COBRA participants whose premiums are tied to the program’s established rates. When rates are set below the level necessary to support actual and projected costs, the Self-Insurance Fund effectively absorbs a portion of those costs, indirectly subsidizing coverage for these participants as well as active employees. Maintaining affordable and competitive employee benefits remains an important objective; however, future rate decisions must also reflect the actual cost of the program. Staff will continue to monitor claims, reserves, and healthcare cost trends during FY 2027, with these factors considered in establishing FY 2028 rates and maintaining the longterm sustainability of the Self-Insurance Program. On a motion by Mr. Pruitt and seconded by Ms. Buchanan, the Board approved the appropriation of $1,750,000 from the Self-Insurance Fund balance as requested by the following vote: AYES: Adams, Buchanan, Cobler, Dillard, Lawless, and Pruitt. NAYS: None. CATEGORICAL TRANSFERS RE: FY 2027 BUDGET RECONCILIATION – SCHOOL BOARD Dale Wagoner, County Administrator, said the School Board is requesting that the Board of Supervisors approve categorical transfers totaling $1,117,751 to reconcile the school's FY 2026-27 budget. At the August meeting, the Board approved amendments to the County FY 2026-27 budget to address the Commonwealth’s budget that was adopted on July 2nd, which included an additional $2.1 million for public education. The School Board is now requesting categorical transfers to place the additional funding in the appropriate categories within its budget: • $35,375 from the Instruction category to the Administration, Attendance and Health category • $380,045 from the Instruction category to the Operations/Maintenance category • $264,248 from the Instruction category to the Technology category • $438,083 from the Instruction category to the Pupil Transportation category On a motion by Ms. Buchanan and seconded by Mr. Dillard, the Board approved the categorical transfers totaling $1,117,751 as requested by the following vote: AYES: Adams, Buchanan, Cobler, Dillard, Lawless, and Pruitt. NAYS: None. ADDITIONAL APPROPRIATION RE: ENGINEERING REPORT – BASSETT BRIDGES LOOP TRAIL Dale Wagoner, County Administrator, said that as part of the ongoing Small Towns Initiative in Bassett, Henry County has received a 50% matching grant from the Harvest Foundation to fund preparation of a Preliminary Engineering Report (PER). The PER will evaluate potential routes and challenges associated with connecting six bridges in Bassett through a loop trail system. Future improvements identified through the PER could be incorporated into the larger Dick & Willie Passage Rail Trail. Staff requests that the Board appropriate $12,500 in grant funds from the Harvest Foundation and $12,500 in matching funds from the Board’s contingency fund, for a total project budget of $25,000. On a motion by Dr. Cobler and seconded by Ms. Buchanan, the Board approved the appropriation of $12,500 from the Harvest Foundation and $12,500 from the Board’s contingency fund for the Bassett Bridges Loop Trail Study by the following vote: AYES: Adams, Buchanan, Cobler, Dillard, Lawless, and Pruitt. NAYS: None. DESIGNATION OF VOTING REPRESENTATIVES FOR THE 2026 VIRGINIA ASSOCIATION OF COUNTIES (VACo) ANNUAL BUSINESS MEETING Dale Wagoner, County Administrator, said the 2026 Virginia Association of Counties (VACo) annual business meeting is scheduled for November 10, 2026. NAYS: None. CONSIDERATION OF THE 2027 LEGISLATIVE AGENDA Dale Wagoner, County Administrator, said staff has prepared a proposed legislative agenda for the Board’s consideration. Each year, staff works with the Board to identify legislative priorities for consideration by the General Assembly. Following the Board’s review and approval, the final agenda will be submitted to Henry County’s General Assembly delegation. On a motion by Ms. Buchanan and seconded by Mr. Pruitt, the Board approved the 2027 legislative agenda and directed it to be sent to our Virginia General Assembly representatives by the following vote: AYES: Adams, Buchanan, Cobler, Dillard, Lawless, and Pruitt. NAYS: None. CONSIDERATION OF A RESOLUTION HONORING J.R. POWELL Mr. Pruitt read aloud a resolution honoring J.R. Powell for his 31 years of service with Henry County. Work Session Meeting King and Queen County Courts and Administration Building First Floor Courtroom Minutes of the Meeting CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL Chairman Mark Berry called the meeting to order. Roll call was taken with all members being present. APPROVAL OF WARRANTS A motion was made by Ms. Alsop and seconded by Ms. Norman to approve the August 24, 2026 warrants subject to audit. AYES: S.C. ALSOP: J.L. SIMPKINS, M. R. BERRY, M.H. NORMAN, C.R. BILLUPS NAYS: NONE ABSENT: NONE DISCUSSION OF BIANNUAL TAX BILLINGS Commissioner of Revenue Kelly Lumpkin and Treasurer Stephanie Sears were present to discuss the processes followed in each of their offices that would be affected by the change from a single billing to biannual billing of real estate taxes. Ms. Lumpkin noted the following items: • Her office would need training and guidance for software training. • There would be hard deadlines for the checking of new construction permits. • The real estate tax rate would also need to be set earlier in April so the calculation could be done for Veteran and Elderly exemptions. • The timeline would leave a small window for her office to get the tax file to the Treasurer’s office for billing. Ms. Sears noted the following items: • It would be double the work for her office. • It would be double the cost for her office. • The cost would increase for inserts. • She feels that it would be a great option for the citizens. • Reminded the board that anyone can prepay their taxes at any time in the year. • Her office would be sending out delinquent notices for June billings. 1 • Since her office provides satellite office hours, it would mean more days with less staff in her office. Mr. Berry noted that since the vehicle decals have been moved to the December billings, that the change to biannual real estate tax billings would not be double the work, it would just replace the work that was eliminated with that change. Ms. Billups questioned how many building permits are reviewed each year and the process. Ms. Lumpkin estimated 150 permits, and she advised that she and her staff go out and review most of them, but some are done by a third party, particularly new home construction and commercial. Ms. Alsop commented that even if it does create more work, it would be a good thing for the citizens. MIDDLE PENINSULA CHESAPEAKE BAY PUBLIC ACCESS AUTHORITY (PAA)APPOINTMENTS Ms. Seay advised that she was recently appointed as the Chair of the PAA. Currently she is the alternate representative and there is no representative. As the Chair, it would be more appropriate for her to be the representative instead of the alternate. Staff is recommending Quentin Mascari to be the alternate representative (if Ms. Seay becomes the representative). A motion was made by Ms. Alsop and seconded by Mr. Simpkins to appoint Ms. Seay as the representative. AYES: S.C. ALSOP: J.L. SIMPKINS, M. R. BERRY, M.H. NORMAN, C.R. BILLUPS NAYS: NONE ABSENT: NONE A motion was made by Ms. Norman and seconded by Ms. Alsop to appoint Quentin Mascari as the alternate representative. AYES: S.C. ALSOP: J.L. SIMPKINS, M. R. BERRY, M.H. NORMAN, C.R. BILLUPS NAYS: NONE ABSENT: NONE VACO CONFERENCE There was brief discussion regarding members that would be attending. The county is allocated three rooms at The Homestead. Mr. Berry, Ms. Billups and Ms. Seay will be using those rooms. Ms. Alsop will also be attending but her room will be covered by VACO since she is a VACO board member. PRESENTATION REGARDING BFI LEASE AMENDMENT REQUEST 2 Ms. Seay provided a Power Point presentation that highlighted the proposed changes included in the amendment requested by BFI. • • • • • • Increase allowable height to match the approved DEQ permit held by the landfill. This would be an increase of 130 feet. Potential reduction in truck traffic related to the removal of leachate from the landfill. Extend the end date of the contract to 2075. A one-time payment of $12 million would be provided to the county. Annual contribution to the school division of .01/ton of waste received. Estimated additional increase of revenue to the county of $60 to $90 million over the life of the expansion. Chairman Berry noted that the presentation will be provided again at the September 14, 2026 meeting. COUNTY ADMINISTRATOR’S COMMENTS Ms. Seay noted that she has received more of the required documents today and that project is continuing to move along albeit very slowly. The responses to the RFQ for the CMR for the elementary school project have been received and are under review. BOARD OF SUPERVISORS COMMENTS Ms. Alsop noted that several board members and the County Administrator attended the VACO Local Officials Summit in Richmond. She was glad the King and Queen was well represented and was able to get information that is important to rural counties to the General Assembly. She also attended the VACO board meeting, and they want each county to do a short movie about the county. She will work with the Director of Communications on this. Mr. Simpkins advised the other board members that there was a very good article in a recent NACO newsletter about data centers and accessory dwelling units. Ms. Norman congratulated the Sheriff on National Night Out success and noted that she hopes the schools will have a great year. Ms. Billups commented that the board has a lot of information and does a lot of research when they are making decisions. She reminded everyone that none of the board members take any decision lightly and they know that they are making decisions that will affect future generations. CLOSED MEETING A motion was made by Ms. Alsop and seconded by Ms. Billups to enter into closed meeting pursuant to Va. Code § 2.2-3711(A)(8) for consultation with legal counsel employed or retained by the Board of Supervisors regarding specific legal matters requiring the provision of legal advice by such counsel, the subject being a claim and request for settlement communicated to County staff. 3 AYES: S.C. ALSOP: J.L. SIMPKINS, M. R. BERRY, M.H. NORMAN, C.R. ALSOP PRESENTATION OF DRAGON RUN STATE FORST TIMBER SALE PROCEEDS – DENNIS GASTON State Forester Dennis Gaston presented the board with a check for $97,742.82. This represents 25% of the proceeds of timber sales from the state forest during FY26 and is payment in lieu of real estate taxes for the land included in the state forest. PUBLIC HEARING – TAVERN MUSEUM LEASE APPROVAL Chairman Berry advised that the lease between the Museum Council and the Board of Supervisors for the Tavern Museum needs to be renewed. In order to do so a public hearing is required. County Administrator Vivian Seay provided proof of publication and background information. Chairman Berry opened the public hearing. Tim Hayes, Bruington – Mr. Hayes stated that he is President of the Historical Society and thanked the board for their continued support of the museum. The museum is celebrating its 25th year in 2026 and the historical society and museum council are excited to continue their relationship with the board. 2 Board members Berry and Billups expressed their thanks to them for the great museum that they provide for the county. A motion was made by Ms. Norman and seconded by Ms. Billups to approve the lease between the Historical Society. AYES: J.L. SIMPKINS, M.R. BERRY, C.R. BILLUPS, M.H. NORMAN NAYS: NONE ABSENT: S.C. ALSOP PRESENTATION – LANDFILL EXPANSION REQUEST/BFI CONTRACT AMENDMENT County Administrator Vivian Seay provided the same presentation that was made at the August 24th meeting which highlighted items that are included in the requested contract amendment. Highlights included: • • • • • • Increase allowable height to match the approved DEQ permit held by the landfill. This would be an increase of 130 feet. Potential reduction in truck traffic related to the removal of leachate from the landfill. Extend the end date of the contract to 2075. A one-time payment of $12 million would be provided to the county. Annual contribution to the school division of .01/ton of waste received. Estimated additional increase of revenue to the county of $60 to $90 million over the life of the expansion. PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD Ann Marie Voight, Stevensville District – Ms. Voight is opposed to the expansion and extending of the contract with BFI. It is difficult to make projections about future tax rates and may not reflect what will happen. Two citizens have been killed by trash trucks and it needs to have an end there should be no more. If the amendment is considered it should be included to change the language from preferred route to required route for trucks going to and from the landfill. The landfill needs to stop allowing parking on Rt. 614. Please speak to the people in the area and find out their concerns. Freddie Byrd, Stevensville District – Asked for confirmation that the contract would be extended for 30 years. What will the CPT be in 30 years? What CPI is used? How was the information about this meeting provided to the public, many elderly people don’t have internet to see it if that is the only way. Something needs to be done about the damage done by vultures on people’s property near the landfill. The landfill was established in 1986 and the host agreement was done in 1992. How will they make sure the leachate doesn’t go into the ground and affect people’s drinking water? Both Wares Church and Second Mount Olive are historic churches in the area, how will this affect the ground that people are buried in at these churches? The landfill was supposed to help the school division and help offset costs to taxpayers. 3 Martha Hart, Buena Vista District – She is concerned about the leachate and the potential environment impacts on historic areas such as the churches. There are lot of unanswered questions. Will the company that treats the leachate always be there? Jeffrey Willacker, Stevensville District – He supports the amendment and feels that it is a win/win for the county. Maybe the county could do something like the City of VA Beach with Mount Trashmore in the future. He hopes the board approves the amendment. Virgie Byrd, Stevensville District – She lives on Mount Olive Road near the landfill and the buzzards are constantly on her house.
