Vice Chair Grech reminded all commissioners and speakers to please turn on and/or speak into the microphones. Mr. Hahn conducted an attendance roll call. Adoption of Agenda Mr. Johnson made a motion to adopt the agenda, as amended. Mr. Adams seconded the motion. The motion passed (4-0). New Business A. Adoption of Minutes: August 25, 2026 Vice Chair Grech allowed time to review the minutes. Mr. Turner made a motion to adopt the minutes, as presented. Mr. Johnson seconded the motion. The motion passed by voice vote, unanimously (4-0). B. Flowerdew Hundred LLC- Special Use Permit Flowerdew Hundred LLC has filed an application for a special use permit (SUP) to construct a self-storage facility located off US Hwy 340, Stanley, VA, and further identified by tax map number 59-(A)-63F. The parcel of land, currently vacant, is located west of Stanley, approximately 0.8 mile north of US HWY BSN 340 W and just to the north of 2845 US Hwy 340 Stanley. The property contains 9.69 acres and is currently zoned as Agriculture (A-1). The applicant is proposing to construct a self-storage facility for up to 500 self-serve storage units in a mix of sizes that are detailed in the narrative. Under Section 125.4 of the Page County Zoning Ordinance, a self-storage facility or a self-storage is defined as a structure or structures containing separate storage spaces of varying sizes leased or rented as individual leases for the purpose of storing personal property and household goods. In the Agricultural Zoning District, pursuant to Section 125.10.19, this requires a special use permit. Ms. Clatterbuck reviewed supplemental regulations in that code section. She noted that this was the first application that staff held a pre-application meeting on, and her opinion was that it was very helpful in helping the applicant understand what staff wants to see up front, and what to expect at the Planning Commission level. She noted they had another pre-application meeting today, and they seem Planning Commission Minutes- September 22, 2026 like they're working well. She reviewed agency comments from VDOT, the Health Department, and the Building Official. She referenced the draft conditions included in the packet. She noted the applicant would be requesting that the Planning Commission consider scheduling it for a public hearing once they have discussed it, tonight. Mr. Hahn noted he would not read the entire Comprehensive Plan review, verbatim, as he doesn’t typically do that. He referenced that the property was in the Agricultural Protection Tier. The purpose of that tier is to protect and to keep from being damaged or lost to agricultural uses, and preserving rural lifestyle and a sense of community that is longer than the defined age count. This tier is intended primarily for low-density residential development, large plot rural development, and agricultural uses. Non-residential uses should serve the needs of residents in the surrounding rural areas, and generally be limited to agricultural businesses. He referenced the policies he cited in the staff memo should match those he has previously cited, and they are from Goal 2, 3, and 6. Goal 6. Policy 6.10 is something he typically includes for commercial types of operations or uses in rural areas. Tax Map 59-(A)-63F is a portion of a larger lot that was divided via 25-acre divisions and non-family divisions, along with a boundary line adjustment, in 2024, as well as court-authorized divisions in 2025. The only residential address located within approximately 500 ft. of Tax Map 59-(A)-63F is 2844 US HWY 340, located on the west side of US HWY 340. 2845 US HWY 340 is the physical address for a poultry structure located approximately 50 ft. from the southwest parcel line of 59-(A)-63F. 2195 US HWY 340 is the address for structures previously operated as Page Valley Flea Market, located within a Commercial (C-1) split-zoned portion of Tax Map 59(A)-40. This split-zoned portion of lot 59-A-40 is approximately 60 ft. from one corner of Tax Map 59-A-63F. Tax Map 59-(A)-63F does not have access to public water or wastewater. Contained within in the application packet is the applicant’s “Comprehensive Plan Compliance Narrative,” which includes a table of policies and consistency analysis of most of the policies listed, above. Planning staff generally concurs with the conclusions represented, here, including the assertion that the Zoning Ordinance reflects “the County’s own determination that a facility of this type can coexist with the district’s agricultural purpose without altering the land’s underlying agricultural zoning or availability for future agriculture use.” Staff notes that “rural character” may be interpreted in different ways. The Comprehensive Plan provides a general framework in Exhibit 5: Development Guidelines; however, a commercial storage land use does not necessarily fit cleanly within the “Rural Business” category. The Zoning Ordinance’s allowance of this use in the Agriculture zoning district by special use permit suggests that Rural Business may be a comparable “Land Use Type” from Exhibit 5. Staff recommends the Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors consider appropriate conditions to address potential adverse impact of this use brought forward during the public hearing(s). Vice Chair Grech invited David Reed to speak regarding the application. Mr. Reed: If you have any questions, I'm glad to get started with those. If you don't have any, I'm glad to give a brief narrative and background. This property, you've seen it in a rezoning request. However, this is a much different request before you today. This is for a special use permit for a particular use. The property also has been site visited, as some of you did. I would encourage you to take another look at the property because it looks a little different than it did during your past site visits. In that regard, this is for a storage facility. It's capped at 10% of the total acreage. Just so you're aware of that, that's under the current regulations. So, that's under Page 2 of 6 Planning Commission Minutes- September 22, 2026 roof capacity, capped at 10%. The applicant can't go over that percentage. In the proposal, this property sits within less than 100 feet from a commercial-zoned property. It sits under a mile from the county's commercial landfill. It sits on one of the two main highways in the county. You can't get better road frontage than this goes in terms of being actually located on one of the two main highways on Route 340. I think this application would look different if it fronted on a much smaller secondary road. In fact, your Comprehensive Plan encourages locating uses like this onto a primary Route 340-211 highway in the county. This has no water, no sewer proposed. The applicant doesn't intend at this time to install any sort of sewage system that will get in the middle of a well. There will be no on-site management. It will be done remotely and come to the property to interact with the renter as needed on a call type basis. That resolves a lot of any concern I would say related to the availability of public water and sewer to the site, which are not available. [It is] not even going to have on-site water or sewer. We'll have onsite electric. The electric unit is already in place. It has been cleared already and is prepared for installation of the actual older electric facility on the ground overhead. That comes from the […] property to the south. That's already in place. Not the actual property, but the unit that will be cleared to connect to the public. The entrance was designed by Racey in 2024. That's when the plan was entered into in agreement with Racey. […] it shows the upfront investment required just to get a plan, an engineer plan that could be submitted to VDOT. You're talking thousands of dollars. Back in 2024, when this kind of concept began from an engineering perspective, VDOT had no objection to the proposal for Racey’s engineering plan. The applicant would construct the engineering compliance with that plan in the VDOT environment. It does require, as I understand it, a paved section, which then converts to a raffled section at a certain distance back off the road as it enters more fully onto the property. Adverse impacts to the neighbors - the closest house is across the road on 340. It's challenging to even see that from the property in that regard. Then you have your business commercial used within 180 feet to the north of the market property area. The mix of units is pretty consistent with this type of facility. I'm glad to answer any questions you have. I’ve given you the details, an improved site, an entrance plan, giving me mitigating factors for water/sewer/traffic. Discussion included the following: • Mr. Adams referenced the summary of why the applicant believes this to be consistent with the Comprehensive Plan. He asked why Mr. Reed thinks it fits in the Protection Tier. Mr. Reed referenced his Comprehensive Plan analysis, and he encouraged them to take a look at that. He stated it goes nearly line by line through the comprehensive plan and details out the analysis related to this particular project. He noted he sat at the Board of Supervisors meeting last night and heard we don't have enough money to pay for the schools we want or have. We're concerned with business income and jobs. This is literally a business asking to come locate in Page County and pay revenue, business license tax, employ someone in some capacity, provide a service, not asking for a grant from the county or the county's donations or money to put this here. That's part of the Comprehensive Plan, as well economic growth, jobs, support for schools. This project has no related school-age children. It doesn't generate housing, which then generates the need for higher education, more schools, etc., for teachers. So this is a net positive in terms of tax revenue and these costs to the county, unlike some projects that you have come before you that may not be able to say that as directly. Mr. Hahn noted that, just speaking for his own review, he does not call out every single policy that could possibly be relevant. Commissioners may find other policies that may speak to this and inform your consideration of the SUP. He noted Page 3 of 6 Planning Commission Minutes- September 22, 2026 • • the same is probably true for [what policies were provided by] the applicant. He also referenced staff maps, including the Farmland map, which indicates this parcel is located on moderate farmland. There was brief discussion about how much of the property remained forested. Some has been cleared, but some still remains. There was discussion of whether the current wooded area would be effective screening from the front. Mr. Reed mentioned challenges with this, as it had been selectively harvested, so you don’t have a traditional evergreen barrier. Ms. Grech referenced the size and number of the buildings, which she thinks is 1,800 linear feet of building, and she wonders if this is compatible with rural character. There was lengthy discussion about the Concept Plan. Ms. Grech and Mr. Johnson both indicated a need for more details on the Concept Plan, including the locations of the buildings. Ms. Grech referenced the issue of proximity to the neighboring confined feeding operation structures, and there was discussion. She asked Ms. Clatterbuck for her opinion. Ms. Clatterbuck indicated agreement with Mr. Reed’s interpretation. We do not define public occupancy in the definitions under 125-4. It could be a different conversation if there was going to be an office and it was going to be staffed. There was discussion regarding how the site would be monitored, as there would not be an office. Mr. Reed described the kind of security cameras that would be used. Mr. Hahn referenced a September 3, 2026 memorandum from the applicant, which provided a summary of position and analysis related to the “inapplicability of the 300-Foot confined feeding operation.” The requested action was that “Staff and the Planning Commission proceed with review and consideration of the Special Use Permit application on the understanding that § 125-10(H) does not apply as a condition of, or barrier to, approval.” Because the meeting was cancelled, and Mr. Hahn had received questions related to this memo, he requested comment from the County Attorney in anticipation of the meeting, tonight. The County Attorney generally that this was about the “public occupancy.” Mr. Hahn noted, regarding the memorandum’s specific request, the County Attorney stated there is no reason not to move the matter forward as it relates to the 300’ of CAFO language. Regarding the need for a condition to clarify an interpretation, the County Attorney stated it was not necessary. There is already a condition that requires compliance with ordinances. Ms. Grech returned to the topic of the site plan. From her perspective, this is the first time in her almost seven years on the Planning Commission that they have seen a Concept Plan with no metrics on it. And since the plan is an intricate part of the special use permit, and needs to be reviewed for substantial compliance, she is wondering if Mr. Reed would consider, now that the 300-foot setback is no longer an issue, giving them some metrics rather than citing the minimum setbacks from the code. Mr. Reed noted he grew up in the poultry industry in Page County. His grandparents had poultry houses. They had one double-decker and three farmhouses. This concept of somehow this is not compatible with a poultry operation, for me as the applicant, that he doesn’t want poultry operations nearby, that is just entirely wrong. That’s an industry he grew up in. His work as an attorney crosses over into that industry on a fairly regular basis in Page County. So, that's a very compatible use with this particular type of specially used storage facility, because you don't have houses, you don't have other types of business located near those facilities. He also noted that the poultry operation is a non-conforming, grandfathered facility that could not be constructed in its current location under the current ordinance. So, if it wasn't there and you wanted to put it there, you wouldn't be able to put it where it's currently located. Also, from a topography perspective, these poultry houses sit generally higher than this property. It kind of slopes downwards. He described the topology further. Ms. Grech stated she was Page 4 of 6 Planning Commission Minutes- September 22, 2026 • skeptical of sending to public hearing a concept plan without any metrics. They have never done that before. That would create, in her opinion, an unfortunate precedent. Generally, from her experience, they have never had a concept plan attached to a special use permit, because it's an integral part of the permit, without metrics. She would like to see a plan with the setbacks, not what the code requires, not the minimum setback. She would like to see the actual setback between the road and the buildings. Mr. Reed indicated that they are not interested in doing that. They just went through a campground SUP recently, where he represented an applicant, and that gentleman spent tens of thousands of dollars on site plans, that ultimately resulted in a full application and no value. He has been discussing this with staff - how much can the Planning Commission ask for in a site plan in terms of details that cost the applicant a considerable amount of money and planning and effort and time. This has been going on since the design of the entrance, since 2024, almost two years. It complies with the minimum requirements. It will probably end up being more than the minimum requirements. Part of the challenge with giving those numbers is the site would need to be more level. Once that is done, that's going to kind of dictate exactly where the building would be located on the north and south ends - how much slope you need to get that to more level. He talked about the excavator. He is very hesitant to give any of the exact numbers that are beyond the minimum because when they put the site pad in, depending on how the slope is, you may end up with a much greater distance on one hand and a much shorter distance on the other. You still need that flexibility to manage the site because there's got to be a leveling of the site. Ms. Grech stated that is precisely the flexibility that allows the Zoning Administrator to interpret whether it's in substantial compliance. Mr. Johnson thanked Mr. Reed for an excellent application - a lot of detail, very well thought out. He stated a special use permit requires them to make specific judgments about certain aspects of a development in a certain place. After lengthy discussion about the general purpose of concept plans and substantial compliance, as well as general discussion of this particular site, Mr. Johnson stated his other significant concern is it's their duty to make sure that the public has enough information to be able to comment on an application like this from the perspective of how it affects their interests. If they don't specify it significantly/closely enough, then he doesn’t think we're serving the public in that regard. He knows it’s a balance. They discussed the draft conditions. There was discussion about the duration. Ms. Grech noted that the previous staff memo recommended 40 years, but this one draft left it blank. Mr. Reed stated certain other nearby and adjoining jurisdictions don't put timelines on special use permits. That is something Page County has chosen to do, but not everyone does it, in terms of counties around us. He thinks they have to look at each application differently in terms of a time limit. This application is a heavy infrastructure investment and physical building cost associated with it that's going to have a long longevity. There's also considerations in talking to a proposed lender for the project, and if you have a duration of the project where it would expire fairly quickly, and in the real estate world fairly quickly is a pretty long period of time, it can have considerations on the ability to get a loan to finance the improvements on the project. It can also have an impact on the appraisal, which is part of the financing process for the project. He requested that they consider a longer period of time that accommodates better the financing of the appraisal and the considerations … She noted there's a lot of talk recently about data centers. If they accept a plan today without any metrics or any sizes, they are opening themselves to having aggressive potential developers, which does not include this applicant and has … in and have privileges provided for in the Page County Zoning Ordinance, and any ordinance amendments for the period set forth within the parameters in this special use permit. TO: FROM: Chairman Thomas and Board of Supervisors Tyler Olsen, Finance Director SUBJECT: DATE: Budget Changes October 19, 2026 Requests The School Board has received $16,865 in insurance proceeds. Rather than requesting an additional appropriation, the School Board is reducing its state revenue estimate to reflect more recent, lower projections. The insurance proceeds will be used for transportation expenses instead of instructional purposes. Accordingly, it is requested that the Instructional category be reduced by $16,865 and the Transportation category be increased by the same amount. The School Board has also incurred various expenses related to repairs and capital projects. Expenses under $7,000 are being absorbed within the existing budget. For the remaining expenses, the School Board is requesting $252,012 from the General Fund Balance, as detailed in the attachment. Purchase orders have been issued for all items except the well drilling and pump at Springfield Elementary School. Two quotes for the well drilling are included in the attachments. Accordingly, it is requested that $252,012 from the General Fund Balance be appropriated to the Operations and Management category to cover these expenses. The General Registrar has received $700 in filing penalty fees. It is requested that these local funds be appropriated for part-time wages in the office. The Sheriff's Office has received $21,001 in grant funding from the DMV. It is requested that these federal funds be appropriated for overtime wages and radar and LIDAR equipment. Recommendation Staff recommends appropriation of all requests. BUDGET CHANGES October 19, 2026 General Fund Balance Update After accounting for $3.5 million in current-year carryovers and appropriations, the estimated General Fund Balance is $16.7 million, or $8.5 million above the growing minimum required balance. Over the next few months, the School Board is expected to request $120,000 for three used school buses and $800,000 for the Technology Center’s welding shop. Beginning in FY 2028, the School Board also anticipates needing an additional $1.2 million annually to cover a four percent pay raise and rising health insurance costs. Given the Board’s priority of keeping taxes low and the significant future costs associated with school facility improvements, careful consideration must be given to the impact of spending decisions on the General Fund Balance. Although the current balance exceeds the required minimum, continued use of these funds without sufficient replenishment could negatively impact the County’s borrowing rates on debt, which will be needed to fund facility improvements. Fiscal Impact The appropriation requests are funded with $252,012 from the General Fund Balance, $700 in local funds, and $21,001 in federal funds. These requests will increase the General Fund Budget by $21,701 and School Operating Fund Budget by $252,012. The School Board’s transfer request will decrease the Instructional category by $16,865 and increase the Transportation category by the same amount. BACKGROUND: On June 17, 2025, the Board of Supervisors held a retreat to discuss a number of topics, one of which was shortterm tourist rentals (STR’s). On September 2, 2025 a joint meeting was held between the Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors to discuss a number of topics, again, one specifically being STR’s. As a result of that joint meeting, the Board of Supervisors established a steering committee to focus on issues related to STR’s. The steering committee met over the course of a few months. On March 2, 2026, Supervisor Cubbage presented findings of the steering committee to the Board of Supervisors. As a result of that discussion, it was the consensus of the Board of Supervisors to send the steering committee’s findings and proposed recommendations to the Planning Commission for further consideration. The draft that came out of the Planning Commission was presented to the Board back on August 3, 2026. In the staff memo dated July 15, 2026 that was introduced to the Board, staff provided a number of recommendations of language to be amended and/or removed due to enforcement concerns. During the introduction meeting, the Board agreed to amend/and or remove the language as staff suggested. The attached draft dated 8/4/26 and the brief description below reflect those changes. BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF PROPOSED AMENDMENTS: The following is a brief overview of the changes as currently drafted: • In Article II (Word Usage and Definitions), amend Section 125-4 (Definitions) as follows: o Add a new definition for “short-term tourist rental, owner-occupied.” Summary: Adding a new definition for owner-occupied STR’s since there is protection in the state code for owner-occupied rentals. • In Article IV (District Regulations), Section 125-9 (Woodland-Conservation), amend Section 125-9.B(7) relating to Bed and Breakfast Establishments and short-term tourist rentals permitted by-right. Summary: In the W-C zoning district, striking STR’s in this line item and creating a separate use since Bed and Breakfast Establishments and STR’s are not the same use. • In Article IV (District Regulations), Section 125-9 (Woodland-Conservation), add Section 125-9.B(8) relating to short-term tourist rentals permitted by-right and adjust numbering. Summary: Adding in the W-C zoning district, the STR use by right if rental contains no more than three bedrooms (subject to the supplemental regulations) and requiring that the rental either have frontage on a public road or the parcel on which the dwelling is located is accessed by a private lane or driveway that serves the rental and no more than two additional dwellings. • In Article IV (District Regulations), Section 125-9 (Woodland-Conservation), add Section 125-9.B(9) relating to “owner-occupied short-term tourist rentals, subject to the provisions of Section 125-30.21 (if • • • • • • • • • • applicable)” and adjust numbering. Summary: Adding in the W-C zoning district, the owner-occupied STR use and section number adjustment. In Article IV (District Regulations), Section 125-9 (Woodland-Conservation) add Section 125-9.D(21) relating to short-term tourist rentals permitted by special use permit. Summary: Adding in the W-C zoning district, the STR use by special use permit if any one or more of the following apply: The rental contains four or more bedrooms and/or the rental is accessed from a private lane or driveway that serves the rental and more than two additional dwellings. In Article IV (District Regulations), Section 125-10 (Agriculture), amend Section 125-10.B(8) relating to Bed and Breakfast Establishments and short-term tourist rentals permitted by-right. Summary: Striking STR’s in this line item and creating a separate use since Bed and Breakfast Establishments and STR’s are not the same use. In Article IV (District Regulations), Section 125-10 (Agriculture), amend Section 125-10.B(9) relating to short-term tourist rentals permitted by-right. Summary: Adding in the A-1 zoning district, the STR use by right if rental contains no more than three bedrooms (subject to the supplemental regulations) and requiring that the rental either have frontage on a public road or the parcel on which the dwelling is located is accessed by a private lane or driveway that serves the rental and no more than two additional dwellings. In Article IV (District Regulations), Section 125-10 (Agriculture), add Section 125-10.B(10) relating to “owner-occupied short-term tourist rentals, subject to the provisions of Section 125-30.21 (if applicable)” and adjust numbering. Summary: Adding in the A-1 zoning district, the owner-occupied STR use and section number adjustment. In Article IV (District Regulations), Section 125-10 (Agriculture) add Section 125-10.D(28) relating to short-term tourist rentals permitted by special use permit. Summary: Adding in the A-1 zoning district, the STR use by special use permit if any one or more of the following apply: The rental contains four or more bedrooms and/or the rental is accessed from a private lane or driveway that serves the rental and more than two additional dwellings. In Article IV (District Regulations), Section 125-11 (Residential), amend Section 125-11.B(12) to read “owner-occupied short-term tourist rentals, subject to the provisions of Section 125-30.21 (if applicable)”. Summary: Adding in the R zoning district the owner-occupied STR use. In Article IV (District Regulations), Section 125-11 (Residential) add Section 125-11.D(9) relating to short-term tourist rentals permitted by special use permit. Summary: Adding in the R zoning district, the STR use by special use permit only. In Article IV (District Regulations), Section 125-12 (Commercial), amend Section 125-12.B(9) by adding “owner-occupied short-term tourist rentals, subject to the provisions of Section 125-30.21 (if applicable).” Summary: Adding in the C-1 zoning district the owner-occupied STR use. In Article IV (District Regulations), Section 125-12 (Commercial), amend Section 125-12.B(13) by adding language to reflect only one single-family detached dwelling is permitted. Summary: Striking existing language in the C-1 zoning district to limit only one single-family detached dwelling be permitted on any lot, tract or parcel of land. In Article V (Supplementary Regulations), Section 125-30.21 (Short-term tourist rentals), multiple amendments through entire section relating to short-term tourist rentals. Summary: Multiple amendments to the supplemental regulations regarding STR’s. Staff would also note that the proposed draft has been reviewed by the County Attorney. text: AGENDA Page County Planning Commission Work Session Board of Supervisors Room- County Government Center 103 South Court Street, Luray, VA 22835 October 27, 2026 - 7:00 p.m. Live Meeting Stream: http://www.pagecounty.virginia.gov/392/Watch-Meetings-Videos ___ Call to Order A. Pledge of Allegiance B. Moment of Silence C. Microphone Reminder D. Attendance Roll Call Adoption of Agenda New Business A. Adoption of Minutes: October 13, 2026 B. Zoning Ordinance Text Amendment- Section 125-54.E(1) Josh Hahn Unfinished Business A. Flowerdew Hundred LLC- Special Use Permit B. Conceptual Plans Discussion C. EDA Housing Subcommittee Report D. Zoning Subcommittee Report Tracy Clatterbuck Tracy & Cassie Josh Hahn Cathy Grech Adjourn MINUTES PAGE COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION October 13, 2026 Members Present Catherine Grech, Vice Chairman, District 1 Jared Burner, Chairman, District 3 Ken Johnson, At-Large Chris Adams, District 2 Sandy Davis, Secretary, District 4 Member Absent William Turner, District 5 Staff Present Josh Hahn Cassie Richards Call to Order Chairman Burner called the October 13, 2026 Page County Planning Commission Regular Meeting to order in the Board of Supervisors (BOS) Room located at the Page County Government Center, 103 S Court Street, Luray, Virginia at 7:00 p.m. The call to order was followed by The Pledge of Allegiance and a Moment of Silence. Chairman Burner reminded all commissioners and speakers to please turn on and/or speak into the microphones. Mr. Hahn conducted an attendance roll call. Adoption of Agenda Ms. Grech made a motion to adopt the agenda as presented. Ms. Davis seconded the motion. The motion passed, unanimously [all ayes]. Citizen Comments on Agenda Items Mr. Hahn noted that four had signed up to speak. Ken Jemielity: It’s been a while. Nice to see you all. I have a couple of concerns about the 25acre rule. I understand the family division. I don’t have a problem if you give your family member a piece of your land to start a house. The five-year split thing sounds reasonable, too. But if I understand the 25-acre rule right, I could take a 150-acre parcel and immediately split it into six 25-acre parcels, and then immediately split it again into twelve, 12.5-acre parcels, and basically create a subdivision without doing any of the infrastructure. That’s my take on it. I don’t know if that’s one hundred percent correct or not. But that just sounds kind of hinky to me. That’s all I have to say about it. Thanks. Chris Anderson: Good evening. Chris Anderson, Alliance for the Shenandoah Valley, whose vision is to inform and engage people to protect natural resources, cultural heritage, and rural character of our region. I am glad that the 25-acre road is being discussed tonight, since it has become the backdoor method of dividing farmland, which was not its original intent. It is time to get this harmful loophole off the books. It is leading to the rapid subdivision of the remaining large parcels of agricultural land in Page County. It is not the farmers who are using this rule for their benefit. It is a way of circumventing the regulations pertaining to Class A and Class B subdivisions. And as a result, we end up with poorly planned subdivisions, and these can be anywhere in the county, not guided towards the towns served by municipal water and sewer. So, yes to allowing the subdivision of land, but follow the process that is there for a reason. As Planning Commission Minutes- October 13, 2026 you all know, the purpose of the subdivision ordinance is to assure the orderly subdivision of land and its development, to realize the wise and full utilization of land resources, to ensure that subdivided lands are reasonably suited for their intended purposes, and to ensure that anything which would detract from the full enjoyment of the subdivided property for its intended purpose be fully and fairly set forth in the plan and to promote the health, safety, convenience, and general welfare of the public. The 25-acre rule does none of these things. The 25-acre rule is just a harmful backdoor method of development. In 2024 and 2025, 25 lots were subdivided under this rule, and they became 89 lots. This is not the direction that Page County needs to be going. But perhaps most importantly, it is in direct conflict with the Comprehensive Plan, which clearly states that we value and want to protect farmland, agricultural operations, our rural character, and our watersheds. Agriculture is Page County's past and future. It is our heritage and main economic driver. That was on full display this past weekend with the Heritage Festival, which was fantastic. The most recent Ag Census determined that Page County has lost 20% of farmland, the most of any county in the Shenandoah Valley. That's a very alarming statistic. There is pressure to rezone Ag land and end up with unplanned residential and commercial development, and our farmland is here. We need to do all that we can to uphold the goals in the Comp Plan and protect our remaining large lots in the county. It is time to close the 25-acre rule, remove it from the Subdivision Ordinance, and protect farmland. Thank you. Beatrice Painter: I want to thank each one of you for letting me say this, because I am a resident of Battle Creek Road, Stanley, Virginia, which is less than a half a mile from the site I believe Mr. Reed is asking for the County to change from Agricultural to Commercial, and I think this lady spoke well of that just a while ago. My sister-in-law Millie Comer, who is present with us today, has lived on the Battlecreek Road for 91 years of her life, except for the one year she and her husband lived in Colorado when he was in the military. So, this is close to us. This isn't property we bought and planned to make money off of it. We bought property to live on. I want to thank you again, and I think this has started since 2025 of September last year, and I think I have made many appearances with the same objections, so I won't read those again tonight because it's the same thing. My objections are based on the safety. The proposed entrance will be hidden by a hill if you're coming from Stanley or Shenandoah, and going to the right-hand turn, you'd be fairly safe with that if they gave you enough space to do that, but if you're coming from Luray, and you make a left-hand turn over this property. As I understand where the road is supposed to be, you're going to have a hill where people come down at least 65 miles an hour. You're going to be passing in front of them. I live on this road. I come out at the old Battlecreek Road to get on the new 211-340, and there are many times that I have almost been hit because I cannot see what's coming over a hill. This Commercial rezoning, or whatever you want to call it, is going to make that a much more dangerous road than it's ever been, and trust me, I see a lot of crosses and a lot of places where people have lost their lives on this section of road. I think I made that point very clear. The second point is the water level, and listen, we need that water. We need it in our community. We have poultry houses in our community. We have homes in our community. Common sense tells you if you have a commercial property there, you're going to be using a whole lot more water than is probably there. I may be wrong on that, but I personally, since I live there, I'm going to take a chance on that, so I'm opposed to this measure. As far as I know, there are no other Commercial properties from Kite's Store at Newport throughout 211 and extending to Food Line Shopping Center. No Commercial properties. All Agriculture and homes, okay? And excluding the County landfill, of course, which, I'll be honest with you, I do not want my neighborhood. It is there. It got there Page 2 of 8 Planning Commission Minutes- October 13, 2026 without my approval, and I tell you, it is a mess. It's a stinking mess, and it's an unsightly mess. It's in my backyard. Ronnie Painter: Good evening. I'm from this area. I've lived there 81 years, and I am totally against changing farmland to Commercial. I was a farmer for over 60 years. Also worked in a factory. [He read from the previous speaker’s document.] People are moving into this area, building homes and having families, and trying to get away from commercial areas for the peace and quiet. Not having a commercial property in their back, or in some cases, in their front yard. From what I know, Mr. Reed's goal is to make more money, and not for the wellbeing of the neighbors. I, for one, speak for my entire family. I do not want an unknown commercial business in our neighborhood. Thank you again for my voice in this concern. [He stopped reading from the document.] Safety. I live right on the road, and I've had some near misses. I'll tell you that. And I consider myself, yet, still a good driver. And this property, he has, he not only has one entrance to the highway, he has two. He owns two pieces of property on both sides, east and west. So, he's going to be in and out of two driveways. And one time, I had two driveways, and I had several near misses with a hay wagon and tractor. See, I have some other things to say, but I'll close my mouth again. But if you have any questions, feel free to ask me about the safety. I'd like to say, my driveway, I can see a lot farther either way, north and south, than Mr. Reed can. Thank you. New Business A. Adoption of Minutes: September 22, 2026 Chairman Burner allowed time to review the minutes. Mr. Hahn noted two changes, which Mr. Johnson had pointed out prior to the meeting. • Page 2, second paragraph, “is longer than the defined age count” should be “has long defined Page County.” Mr. Hahn indicated this was a missed AI transcription error. • Page 3, toward end of continuing paragraph, “raffled” should be “graveled.” Mr. Johnson made a motion to adopt the minutes, as amended. Ms. Grech seconded the motion. Chairman Burner asked Mr. Hahn to conduct a roll call. The motion passed, unanimously (50). B. Conceptual Plan Discussion Ms. Richards referenced a proposed definition and requirements for a conceptual development plan. This basis of the draft basically comes from the Zoning Subcommittee, with staff recommendations based on previous meetings. Because Ms. Clatterbuck was not present, she recommended Planning Commissioners review the draft on their own time, and discuss at a later meeting. She welcomed any comments they had. Ms. Grech noted this was something the Zoning Subcommittee had spent some time on about a year ago. This is a pretty good summary – well done. Unfinished Business A. Flowerdew Hundred LLC- Special Use Permit Mr. Hahn clarified that this is not a rezoning application. There is a rezoning application involved with this property that is still before the Board, currently on hiatus. This is a separate application specifically for storage facilities involving the same parcel. He noted that the packet included an updated conceptual development plan. He noted that he had himself created the base map, which was scaled and shows general setbacks. His elements are included in the Page 3 of 8 Planning Commission Minutes- October 13, 2026 legend, and then he provided the base map to the applicant. He stated that if Commissioners had any questions specific to items described in the margin, they should address that to the applicant. He also referenced updated conditions that are included in the packet. He referenced an email he had forward with a public comment related to this application. He noted the date a public hearing could be scheduled. He also noted three Commissioners had visited the site with Mr. Reed since the last meeting: Ms. Grech, Mr. Johnson, and Ms. Davis. Ms. Grech confirmed she had visited the site. Mr. Reed was very gracious to take us around and show us everything. There's been a lot of clearing. All the trees that were there are gone. It's basically totally deforested on the area that's at the front of the property. She was surprised by a couple of things in the package tonight. First of all, there was a consensus at the September 22nd meeting to choose a period of 40 years for the SUP. She doesn’t know why that wasn't reflected, because that was a consensus. Another thing that surprised her is there are six buildings on the previous plan, seven on this one. We have a new born building. She thinks that's a little much. Six is already six times 300 feet, 1,800 linear feet. This puts it to 2,100 linear feet with really not many setbacks on the side, 20 on one side, and 21 on the other. There was lengthy discussion about the number of buildings and widths between them. Mr. Hahn noted he had calculated the number of buildings and dimensions, and this is still under the 10% limit of lot coverage. Ms. Grech stated she doesn’t dispute that, but this is a lot of buildings, and she is surprised to see a new one pop up. Some of them are pretty narrow, 10 feet and 20 feet. Only one is 30 feet, so they're not extremely wide. He doesn't have any 40-foot buildings. So, we need to change that metric of 40 in condition seven to 30. She noted previous discussion that there should be a condition regarding appearance or color scheme, requiring neutral colors. She thought it was Mr. Adams. She thinks that would be good, conforming with rural character. There was discussion about adding trees to the front of the property. Discussion included the concern that with a green belt of trees, the overgrowth of those trees is eventually going to block the site distance coming out of there, and then they are going to cut them down anyway, because they hang over. Chairman Burner asked if there is going to be security fencing around the property, or at least the storage units, to control egress and ingress, considering they are going to have security cameras up front. Mr. Reed came forward to the podium. He stated that during the site visit that was conducted, there was a discussion where there would be a gate set back far enough from the road to allow a very good pull-off distance, but that with the topography along the road in particular, it really doesn't allow multiple entrances onto the road from a topography perspective. And then the one section of the property, the northern boundary, is fenced already, and the southern boundary has a pretty good slope to it that will likely be increasing when there's a pad installed. And then the back section of the property to the east, furthest from 340, is not part of the proposed area. There was further discussion about fencing, but no agreement that this should be a condition. There was also further discussion about trees, but no agreement that this should be a condition. Ms. Grech asked if he would consider maybe planting a few trees along that blue line shown on the concept plan. Mr. Reed was concerned about site distance requirement from VDOT. There was discussion about a new condition regarding color palette. Mr. Hahn suggested some language, requiring construction material using a neutral color palette. He noted that Ms. Richards recalled a condition from a previous campground SUP that refers to color palette, Page 4 of 8 Planning Commission Minutes- October 13, 2026 which staff could review. Ms. Grech also requested the width of the buildings be 30 instead of 40, and that the SUP be limited to a term of 40 years in the draft conditions. Ms. Grech made a motion to send this to public hearing at the next available date. Mr. Johnson seconded the motion. Ms. Grech clarified the date would be November 10. Chairman Burner requested a roll call vote. The motion passed, unanimously (5-0). B. Subdivision of Land Discussion Mr. Hahn reminded the Commission that they spent quite some time at the last meeting going over all the definitions, as well as resequencing some of the components of the overall ordinance. He’d like to focus on the four exceptions listed under the definition of SUBDIVIDE, which includes boundary line adjustments, 25-acre rule divisions, non-family divisions, and family divisions. Subsequent discussion was mostly related to 25-acre divisions, and how boundary line adjustments and non-family divisions may be used in tandem with 25-acre divisions. Mr. Hahn indicated that there are no significant changes currently proposed to the substance of the family or non-family division provisions. The Commission had previously considered increasing the required ownership period associated with family divisions but reached consensus not to change the existing time period. Staff may clarify the family division provisions regarding who qualifies as a family member and how ownership by corporations or other entities interacts with the family division provisions. Staff also intends to consolidate plat requirements applicable to the various administrative divisions into a common section rather than repeating substantially similar requirements under each type of division. The initial proposed changes related to 25-acre divisions are intended address some of the concerns associated with the existing 25-acre division provision. Under the initial proposal: • All parcels resulting from a 25-acre division would continue to contain at least 25 acres and have at least 20 feet of legal access. • Neither a parcel created through a 25-acre division nor its parent parcel could be further divided using the 25-acre provision for five years. • During that five-year period, a parcel created through the provision could not be reduced below 25 acres through a boundary line adjustment, recombination, or subsequent division. • The five-year restriction would run with the land and would not be eliminated through a change in ownership. • Entrances onto public roads would remain subject to VDOT requirements. The main effect of this approach would be to slow the current sequence of divisions, rather than permanently limit the number of divisions that could ultimately occur. A large parcel could still initially be divided into as many 25-acre parcels as its acreage would permit, but the resulting parcels could not immediately be reduced below 25 acres or reused for additional 25acre divisions. Commissioners expressed concern that the initial proposal did not go far enough. The principal objection was that imposing a five-year waiting period would delay, rather than prevent, the pattern of successive divisions that has caused concern. Page 5 of 8 Planning Commission Minutes- October 13, 2026 The Commission discussed the existing 25-acre provision as an unusually powerful exception because a landowner can create as many 25-acre parcels as the original acreage permits and then combine the provision with boundary line adjustments and other division methods. This can allow a large Agricultural parcel to be converted into numerous smaller residential parcels without proceeding through the Class A or Class B subdivision process. The concern was therefore not simply the creation of 25-acre parcels. Rather, it was the cumulative use of the 25-acre division, boundary line adjustments, and subsequent non-family divisions to create what Commissioners characterized as de facto or “wildcat” subdivisions outside the normal subdivision process. Commissioners emphasized that the County's responsibility is to provide for the orderly subdivision of land and expressed concern that substantial subdivision activity is currently occurring through exceptions to the subdivision regulations rather than through the Class A and Class B procedures themselves. An alternative direction proposed by Chairman Burner was discussed: permitting a one-time use of the 25-acre division for a parent tract. Under this concept, a landowner could use the 25acre provision once and could create as many qualifying parcels during that division as the acreage of the parent parcel permits. Call to Order Chair Hughes called the meeting to order. 2. Invocation Mr. Hatcher led the invocation. 3. Adoption of Agenda Request to postpone action, amend, or approve Agenda as presented Ms. Bowlin made a motion to the agenda as presented. Mr. Hall seconded. All AYEs. MOTION PASSED VOTE 5-0 4 4. Administrative Items a. Minutes from August 4, 2026 regular Planning Commission meeting Ms. Winall mentioned that Mr. Hall did the invocation. Mr. Hatcher made a motion to approve the minutes as amended. Ms. Bowlin seconded the motion. All AYEs. MOTION PASSED VOTE 5-0 5. Public Comment Period Chair Hughes opened the public comment period. Carl Schwendeman, 1727 Theresa Lane, stated that Powhatan County did not receive the TAP grant. He also asked if the County could oppose the natural gas plant in Cumberland County. Chair Hughes closed the public comment period. 6. Public Hearings a. 26-06-REZ-C: Evans Realty LLC & Holly Hills Holdings LLC (District 1/Flat Rock) Request to rezone 15.39 acres on Tax Map Parcels 42-73, 42-75, and 4323A from Agricultural-10 (A-10) to Light Industrial (I-1), with proffered conditions. The parcels are located on the north side of Anderson Highway between Holly Hills Road and Dogwood Road and include 1650 Anderson Highway. The County’s Comprehensive Plan designates the properties as Gateway Business and within the Route 60 Corridor East Special Area Plan. Sean Clendening presented the case including information on the Future Land Use Map, the conceptual development, buffering, traffic impact, proffers, and entrances. 5 Anne Miller, applicant, gave an overview of the project and addressed proffers and entrance concerns. Ms. Winall asked if there was consideration for increasing the buffer on the residential properties. Ms. Miller stated that they haven’t had a chance to fully evaluate the issue with the owner, but they are amenable to additional buffering. Ms. Bowlin asked about the size of the buffer that the Gateway project had. Brian Haney stated that the buffer distance is 75 feet; however, 45 feet of it is on the residential part. Ms. Miller said that they do not own the residential and can’t match that situation. Ms. Winall asked about the front buffering and if that had been considered. Ms. Miller asked if this was related specifically to outdoor storage or if there was a concern with a use adjacent to the residential properties. Mr. Hall stated that he believed the 30 feet and the additional 20 would be best. Ms. Miller stated that the 30 foot buffer and the 20 feet would be agreeable. Chair Hughes opened the public comment period. Carl Schwendeman, 1727 Theresa Lane, asked if the developer could close the second entrance on Route 60 and use a cross access, and if the developer could add a sidewalk along the front of the property. Chair Hughes closed the public comment period. Mr. Hatcher stated his concern about access and the effect on the public regarding accidents on Route 60. Mr. Hall stated that the connection between parcels is important, but also mentioned that owners have property rights, and hoped that the owners would address the concerns. Ms. Winall stated that she does not support the three entrances and asked about a clause that states they will do their best effort to ensure the cross access. 6 Ms. Jackson stated that these conversations should have already occurred and that it is up to the applicant to amend their application if they would like to present it that way. Ms. Bowlin stated that she doesn’t like the entrances so close to each other but doesn’t see a solution. Mr. Haney stated that the intent of staff is to require interparcel connectivity. Mr. Hatcher stated that if Powhatan is not concerned with the singular entrance, VDOT may not be concerned either. Mr. Hall stated that he hopes the applicant gets the entrance issue is resolved before it gets to the Board of Supervisors. Mr. Hall made a motion to approve the rezoning with the amended proffers. Ms. Winall seconded the motion. Mr. Hall, Ms. Bowlin, Ms. Winall, Mr. Hughes voted AYE. Mr. Hatcher voted NAY. MOTION PASSED VOTE 4-1 7. Other/Misc. Items a. Board of Supervisors Referral: Resolution R-2026-53 Referring Zoning Ordinance Text Amendment to Planning Commission for 2026 State Law Updates related to Solar Facilities, High Energy Use Facilities, Manufactured Homes, Off-Street Parking and Loading, and Family Day Homes Mr. Haney provided an overview of the ordinance amendments. Mr. Hatcher asked about Bed and Breakfast Homes in Rural Residential. Ms. Winall explained that they were moved to Accessory Uses. Mr. Hatcher stated that he believes they should be more of a Conditional Use than an Accessory Use. Ms. Jackson stated that it would be a change from how it is treated currently. Ms. Winall mentioned a landscaping company in RR. Ms. Jackson stated that Rural Residential is an older zoning district and terms needed updating. 7 Mr. Hatcher brought up that Village Residential isn’t in the Future Land Use map. Ms. Jackson stated it may be worth discussing during the comprehensive plan update, but Village Residential is in the ordinance currently. Ms. Winall asked if solar needed to be added to the Office zoning district. Ms. Jackson stated she would verify whether it needed to be added. Mr. Hatcher asked about some of the new names in the definitions. Ms. Jackson stated that the purpose of the name changes was to match the terms used in state law. Mr. Hatcher asked if anyone was aware of solar facility power transferred by heat. Ms. Bowlin asked if any other counties are using the term solar farm. Ms. Jackson stated that she didn’t see it for the counties she looked at. Ms. Winall asked if the use standards that were in bold were being added. Ms. Jackson answered affirmatively and stated that staff need to add use standards for that section. Ms. Winall asked if the added sections came from state requirements. Ms. Jackson stated that section came from state standards. Mr. Hughes asked about seeing the revisions indicated clearly. Mr. Haney stated that they would be marked clearly for what changes are occurring. Ms. Winall asked what constitutes a permanent foundation for manufactured homes. Ms. Jackson stated they would need to speak with the Building Official. Ms. Winall asked if there is a reason some use standards were removed. Ms. Jackson stated that there the changes were made to meet state requirements and she would check again. Ms. Winall asked about skirting on manufactured homes. Ms. Jackson stated that they are trying to get a manufactured home to match that of our building code with modular homes. Mr. Hall asked about modular homes with a permanent chassis and its skirting. Ms. Bowlin added that modular was similar to a stick built but constructed offsite and brought in. 8 Mr. Hall said he did not want to see a loophole where someone comes in without a block foundation. Mr. Hatcher asked about requirements for decommissioning solar sites. Ms. Jackson clarified that they could move where they mention those standards. Ms. Winall asked about Rural Residential ADU requirements. Ms. Jackson explained that the chart and use standards now match a previous ordinance amendment from 2024 to be 50%. Ms. Winall questioned whether you could have a manufactured primary residence with a site-built accessory dwelling. Ms. Jackson stated that situation could occur. Ms. Winall asked about a strikethrough issue. Ms. Jackson added that they want to remove the utility scale language from the definition. Mr. Hatcher asked about addressing agrivoltaics. Ms. Jackson stated that nothing about agrivoltaics was mandated. 8. Adjournment Chair Hughes adjourned the meeting. PATTERN BOOK Planning Commission II. October 6, 2026 IDENTIFICATION AND LOCATIONAL INFORMATION Request: Pattern Book Review for Depot at Fighting Creek Existing Zoning: Village Center-Planned Development (VC-PD) Parcel Size: 9.76 acres Parcel Tax Map: 26B1-1-10 Applicant: Brady Deal, Main Street Homes Owner: MFR Fighting Creek LLC Property Location: 4011 Old Buckingham Road Electoral District: District 4 2021 Future Land Use Plan: Gateway Business 1|Page 11 III. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY Project Description The applicant requests Pattern Book approval for the residential portion of a mixed-use development consisting of ten for-rent, triplex Figure 1: Site Location townhome dwellings. The request is associated with the approved rezoning case, 21-01-REZ. The Depot at Fighting Creek is located south of Anderson Highway along Old Buckingham Road west of Mann Road. The property is zoned VC-PD and is designated Gateway Business in the County’s Future Land Use Plan. This request is related to the residential buildings. Three planned commercial buildings will be reviewed individually through the Pattern Book approval process at the time of building permit application. This process will ensure that future commercial development is consistent with the overall architectural character and design standards established for The Depot at Fighting Creek. The proposed residential buildings will be oriented with their primary entrances and front façades facing internal streets. Each residential building will contain two 1,323-square-foot units and one 1,376square-foot unit, for a total area of 4,022 square feet per building. Project Location Figure 2: Site Layout Design Evaluation Pattern Book approval from the Planning Commission is required prior to site plan approval and building permit submittal for Institutional, Commercial, and Mixed-Use Developments. The project’s consistency with the Comprehensive Plan, the Countywide Development Guidebook, and ordinance requirements are determined through evaluation of written descriptions and graphics submitted by the applicant. A summary of the applicable standards from these documents and a description of how the residential buildings for this project comply are outlined in Table 1, below. 2|Page 12 Because the development includes both residential units and commercial pad sites, the Pattern Book should establish a cohesive architectural theme that unifies the design of all buildings throughout the development. The applicant has submitted The Depot at Fighting Creek Architectural Design Guidelines, dated August 10, 2026. The standards set forth in these guidelines are compared with Pattern Book Standards for Institutional, Commercial, and Mixed-Use Development which are outlined in Table 2 below. These guidelines are intended to establish consistent architectural standards for the development and will be used in the review of future Pattern Book applications to ensure that the commercial buildings complement the approved residential development and maintain a cohesive overall design throughout The Depot at Fighting Creek. Table 1: Pattern Book Standards Multifamily and townhouse development standards in village growth area districts (83-476) Design Standard Requirement Proposed Related Features Materials & general design Match conceptual plan exhibits per 2101-REZC proffered condition #2. See requirements in Table 2 below. Complies. The proposed provided elevations do generally match the Conceptual Architectural Exhibits dated 17-2021 in rezoning case 21-01-REZ. The proposed colors are white and a grey/brown for the window trim and roofs. (e) Building orientation and configuration. 1. To the maximum extent practicable, buildings shall be configured so that their primary facade and primary entrances orient towards: a. An abutting internal or external street; or b. Common open space, such as interior courtyards, parks, or on-site natural areas or features with a clearly defined and easily accessible pedestrian circulation system. Complies. Based on the conceptual plan, the proposed buildings are configured with their primary facades and entrances oriented toward the internal street network. Final compliance with the building orientation and configuration standards will be confirmed through each residential building permit review. 2. Upper-story dwelling units in a multifamily building shall be accessed via internal corridors, 3|Page 13 common stairways, or individual stairways. (f) Maximum building size in 1. In the Village Center (VC) district, village center districts. individual structure footprints shall not exceed a maximum of 15,000 square feet and total building area shall not exceed 45,000 square feet. 2. The maximum length of any multifamily or townhouse structure shall be 250 feet, regardless of the number of units. (g) Facade articulation. Adjournment Page 2 of 2 POWHATAN COUNTY DEPARTMENTAL POLICY Policy Number: DPU-2026-01 Supersedes: N/A Date Issued: est. 10-08-2026 Department: Public Utilities Subject: Private Pump Stations Standard for Progressive Cavity Grinder Pumps in Low-Pressure Force Main Connections Reference: County Code Sec. 80-129 - Use of private wastewater facilities or pump stations. Criteria The use of grinder pump/low-pressure sewer systems shall be evaluated on a case-by-case basis and shall be in accordance with State laws and regulations, County Code, and these Standards. Where Standards of the County are more stringent than those imposed by the State, the County Standards shall apply. The use of grinder pump systems may be authorized by the County upon a determination that conditions or circumstances exist preventing the use of other approved means of domestic sanitary sewage disposal. 1. Purpose This standard establishes requirements for the selection, installation, operation, and maintenance of progressive cavity (semi-positive displacement) grinder pump systems used in low-pressure wastewater force main systems in Powhatan County to ensure efficient operation, system compatibility, and compliance with local and state regulations, while maintaining private ownership of pump stations. 2. Scope This standard applies to all progressive cavity grinder pump systems installed for wastewater conveyance into force mains within Powhatan County, including new installations and replacements in residential, commercial, or low-pressure sewer systems. All grinder pumps and associated laterals on private property shall be privately owned and maintained. Grinder pump systems shall not be installed and used in lieu of gravity sewer where gravity sewer is available and feasible. 1 3. Definitions • • • • • Progressive Cavity Grinder Pump: A semi-positive displacement pump utilizing a helical rotor and elastomeric stator, equipped with an integral grinding mechanism designed to macerate domestic wastewater solids into a fine slurry and discharge at near-constant flow rates across varying head pressures. Approved Equal: Equipment, materials, or devices determined by the County Engineer to be equivalent in quality, performance, reliability, and functionality to specified standards. Force Main: A pressurized pipeline conveying wastewater from a pump station or grinder pump to a treatment facility, gravity sewer, or another system component. VDEQ: Virginia Department of Environmental Quality. Combination Isolation/Check Valve Assembly: An integrated or paired check valve and isolation shutoff valve assembly designed specifically for low-pressure sewer service lateral connections at the property boundary. 4. Pump Selection & Performance Criteria 4.1 General Requirements All grinder pumps shall be of the progressive cavity (semi-positive displacement) type with steep head-capacity curves to prevent flow starvation when discharging into common low-pressure force mains. Centrifugal grinder pumps are not permitted without express written approval from the County Engineer. 4.2 Residential Performance • • • Flow & Head: Minimum pump rating of 9 GPM at 138 feet total dynamic head (TDH), or as dictated by system hydraulic analysis. Motor Specs: 1 HP (minimum), 240V, single-phase, 60 Hz, 1,725 RPM, continuous-duty rated, oil-filled motor with thermal overload protection. Grinding Mechanism: Heavy-duty, high-hardness (minimum 55 Rockwell C) cutter mechanism capable of shredding typical domestic sewage solids into a fine slurry without clogging. 4.3 Commercial & Multi-Family Units • • Must be sized based on peak design flow rates calculated by a licensed Professional Engineer in the Commonwealth of Virginia. Commercial and multi-family installations must utilize duplex or multiplex pump configurations. 4.4 Basin / Tank Specifications • Capacity: Minimum 70-gallon capacity for standard single-family residential applications to provide adequate emergency storage. 2 • Material: Corrosion-resistant high-density polyethylene (HDPE) or fiberglass-reinforced polyester (FRP). 5. Electrical and Control Requirements • • • • Power Supply: Pumps shall be connected to a dedicated 240V, 1-phase, 60 Hz electrical branch circuit with a dedicated 30-amp breaker in the main electrical panel of the structure. Alarm Panel: An approved NEMA 4X (weatherproof) visual and high-decibel audible alarm panel must be installed in a conspicuous location visible from the primary driveway or service approach. Control Wiring: Alarm control circuits must be wired to a separate 15-amp breaker from the pump motor breaker to ensure alarm functionality during a pump electrical fault or breaker trip. Disconnection: An external, weatherproof, lockable safety disconnect switch shall be located within direct line-of-sight and within 50 feet of the grinder pump basin. 6. Installation and Connection Standards • • • • Basin Placement: Tanks shall be installed outdoors in an accessible location outside the structure, buried to the manufacturer’s specified depth, and graded to direct surface runoff away from the basin lid. Buoyancy Mitigation: High groundwater areas require concrete anti-flotation ballast rings or ballast anchoring calculated and installed per manufacturer specifications. Discharge Piping: Private service lateral piping from the pump basin to the County force main must be a minimum 1.25-inch or 1.5-inch SDR 11 / SDR 17 HDPE with heat-fused joints, or Schedule 80 PVC with solvent-welded joints. Check Valves & Shutoffs: A redundant check valve shall be located inside the pump basin. An approved combination redundant check valve and isolation ball valve assembly (or approved equal) housed in a meter box must be installed at the property line or public rightof-way boundary to isolate the private lateral and prevent main line backflow. 7. Operation, Maintenance, and Ownership Responsibilities 7.1 Owner Responsibility Property owners bear 100% of the cost for electrical service, preventive maintenance, clearing blockages, mechanical repairs, electrical component replacement, and complete unit replacements. 7.2 Maintenance Agreement & Recorded Covenant (Appendix A) • Required Execution: Prior to final utility approval or building permit sign-off, the property owner must execute and record a formal Grinder Pump Operation, Maintenance, and Indemnification Agreement in the Powhatan County Circuit Court land records. 3 • • Covenant Running with the Land: This agreement constitutes a restrictive covenant that runs with the land, binding all current and future property owners, heirs, and assigns to the ongoing maintenance obligations of the private grinder pump system. Disclosure at Property Transfer: Property owners must disclose the existence of the grinder pump system and the recorded covenant to prospective buyers prior to the transfer of ownership. 7.3 Utility Right of Entry & Emergency Abatement • • Right of Entry: The recorded agreement grants Powhatan County Department of Public Utilities personnel or authorized agents the explicit right to enter private property to inspect the basin, control panel, electrical disconnect, and property-line valve assembly upon reasonable notice (or immediately during an active spill or emergency overflow). County Emergency Action: If a private pump system experiences a breakdown, overflow, or failure that threatens public health or the public force main, and the property owner fails to mitigate the failure within 24 hours of notification, the County reserves the right—but not the obligation—to enter the property, perform emergency pump-outs or repairs, and bill all direct, operational, and administrative costs directly to the property owner's utility bill or record a tax lien against the property. 7.4 Prohibited Discharges No person shall discharge stormwater, foundation drains, sump pumps, industrial chemicals, heavy grease, petroleum products, diapers, personal wipes (including those marketed as "flushable"), feminine hygiene products, or toxic substances into the grinder pump system. 8. Inspection and Testing Protocols • • • Hydrostatic Pressure Testing: Prior to backfilling and final service connection, the installer must subject the private service lateral to a hydrostatic pressure test of 1.5 times the design operating pressure or 100 PSI (whichever is greater) for a minimum of 2 hours with zero allowable leakage. Open Tank Inspection: A County representative must inspect the open excavation to verify proper basin leveling, structural anchoring/ballasting, and pipe bedding materials prior to burial. Startup Verification: A formal startup test using clean water must be performed to confirm proper pump rotation, float switch functionality, low-level shutoff, manual override switches, and visual/audible alarm operation before utility sign-off. 9. Emergency Response & Power Outage Protocols • Extended Power Outages: In the event of a power outage lasting longer than 24 hours, the property owner must strictly limit water usage to essential needs to prevent basin overflow, as the pump will not operate without electrical power. 4 • • Generator Compatibility: Property owners are strongly encouraged to maintain a manual transfer switch or generator receptacle compatible with a minimum 5kW generator to supply emergency power to the pump panel during power failures. Emergency Overflow: If an overflow is imminent and power cannot be restored, the owner must contract with a licensed septage hauler to pump out the basin and transport the wastewater to an authorized disposal facility. 10. Standard Utility Drawings All installations must strictly adhere to County Standard Details or approved manufacturer engineering schematics meeting these parameters. • • • • Detail GP-1: Typical Progressive Cavity Grinder Pump Basin Installation o Bedding Base: Minimum 6-inch compacted rounded aggregate (gravel) bedding base. o Ballast Anchor: Concrete anti-flotation ballast ring detailing minimum concrete volume based on local site groundwater conditions. o Finished Grade: Tank cover must sit a minimum of 2 to 4 inches above final grade, with surrounding soil sloped away from the lid. o Gravity Inlet: 4-inch DWV PVC gravity inlet pipe entering the tank via a flexible EPDM grommet or hub connection. Detail GP-2: Service Lateral and Property Line Connection o Pipe Transition: Outlines the physical transition from the pump discharge line to the HDPE private service lateral. o Valve Housing: Placement of the property-line combination check valve and isolation valve inside an approved plastic or polymer meter box at the property line/right-of-way boundary. o Cleanout: A vertical cleanout assembly extending to grade on the property owner's side of the boundary valve box. Detail GP-3: Electrical Schematics & Disconnect Configuration o Conduit Paths: Independent conduit pathways from the building electrical panel to the outdoor NEMA 4X control/alarm enclosure. o Disconnect Box: An outdoor, lockable safety disconnect switch mounted securely on a pressure-treated post or building exterior wall. o Line of Sight: Maximum 50-foot direct line-of-sight requirement from the disconnect switch to the basin lid. Detail GP-4: Duplex Pump Layout (Commercial/Multi-Family Only) o Basin Scale: Dual or multiplex pump configurations housed inside an expanded diameter basin sized for peak design capacity. o Manifold Block: Independent discharge lines from each pump combining into a unified manifold with separate check and isolation valves for each unit. o Control Alternator: Wiring diagram demonstrating alternating control panel logic to balance runtime across both pump units and activate the lag pump under high inflow conditions 5 11. Policy Revision and Amendment The Director of Public Utilities reserves the right to amend, alter, or revoke any technical provision of this policy to safeguard public health, ensure environmental compliance, or protect the integrity of the County’s public infrastructure. 6 APPENDIX A Tax Map Parcel ID No.: ___ Prepared by and return to: ___ ___ ___ GRINDER PUMP OPERATION, MAINTENANCE, AND INDEMNIFICATION AGREEMENT (Covenant Running with the Land) THIS OPERATION, MAINTENANCE, AND INDEMNIFICATION AGREEMENT (the “Agreement”) is made and entered into this ___ day of ___, 20 __, by and between ___ (whether one or more, the “Owner”), and the COUNTY OF POWHATAN, VIRGINIA, a political subdivision of the Commonwealth of Virginia (the “County”). WITNESSETH: WHEREAS, the Owner is the fee simple owner of certain real property located in Powhatan County, Virginia, more particularly described as Tax Map Parcel No. ___, located at ___ (the “Property”); and WHEREAS, the Owner desires to connect the sanitary sewage system on the Property to the Powhatan County low-pressure wastewater force main system using a private progressive cavity grinder pump station; and WHEREAS, the Powhatan County Department of Public Utilities Standard for Progressive Cavity Grinder Pumps requires that all private grinder pump systems, including tanks, pumps, electrical controls, panels, service laterals, and property-line valve assemblies, be privately owned, operated, and maintained by the property owner; and WHEREAS, the County requires this Agreement to be executed and recorded in the Land Records of the Circuit Court of Powhatan County, Virginia, as a covenant running with the land to ensure the continuous and proper operation, maintenance, and repair of the private grinder pump system. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein and the approval by the County to connect the Property to the public force main sewer system, the Owner hereby covenants, agrees, and declares as follows: 1 1. Ownership and Boundary of Responsibility 1.1 The Owner acknowledges and agrees that the entire grinder pump system—including, but not limited to, the basin/tank, pump core, float/level controls, internal piping, check valves, electrical control panel, alarm enclosure, power feed, outdoor disconnect switch, service lateral piping, and property-line combination check/isolation valve box assembly (collectively, the “Private System”)—is and shall remain 100% private property. 1.2 The County shall have no ownership interest in, nor any obligation to operate, inspect, service, repair, or replace any portion of the Private System. 2. Owner’s Maintenance and Operational Duties 2.1 Continuous Maintenance: The Owner, at their sole expense, shall keep the Private System in continuous good operating condition in strict accordance with the manufacturer's specifications and County standards. 2.2 Prohibited Discharges: The Owner shall strictly prohibit the discharge of stormwater, roof/foundation drains, sump pumps, petroleum products, heavy grease, industrial chemicals, diapers, sanitary wipes (including those marketed as “flushable”), feminine hygiene products, or toxic/flammable substances into the Private System. 2.3 Power Outage Requirements: During electrical power outages, the Owner shall limit water consumption to essential needs to avoid basin overflows. The Owner is encouraged to maintain emergency backup power (such as a portable generator compatible with the pump control panel). 2.4 Repairs, Replacements, and County Notification: In the event of a mechanical, electrical, or structural failure of the Private System, the Owner shall immediately engage a qualified technician or licensed contractor to repair or restore the system to full operating condition. • • • Notification Requirement: The Owner shall notify the Powhatan County Department of Public Utilities in writing (or via the County’s official utility reporting portal) within forty-eight (48) hours of any major repair, pump core replacement, basin structural modification, or control panel replacement. Approved Equipment Only: Any replacement pump, panel, or valve assembly must strictly conform to current County standards (progressive cavity / semi-positive displacement design matching approved hydraulic curves). Centrifugal grinder pumps or unapproved core replacements are strictly prohibited. Right to Re-Inspect: The County reserves the right to conduct a follow-up startup test and open-basin inspection following any complete pump unit or control panel replacement prior to the station being placed back into permanent service. 3. Right of Entry and Inspection 3.1 The Owner hereby grants to Powhatan County, its officers, employees, agents, and contractors, the irrevocable right to enter upon the Property at any reasonable time for the 2 purpose of inspecting the Private System, verifying electrical disconnect line-of-sight, or assessing system compliance. 3.2 Except in the case of an active spill or emergency, the County shall make reasonable efforts to provide prior notice to the Owner before entering the Property for routine inspections. 4. Emergency County Abatement and Cost Recovery 4.1 In the event the Private System experiences a failure, blockage, or overflow that results in (or poses an imminent threat of) an environmental discharge, sanitary sewer overflow (SSO), or hazard to public health and safety, the Owner shall take immediate action to mitigate the discharge. 4.2 If the Owner fails to initiate corrective action or cease the discharge within twenty-four (24) hours of written or oral notification from the County (or immediately in an acute emergency), the County or its contractors shall have the right—but not the obligation—to enter the Property and take all necessary steps to abate the emergency. Abatement actions may include, but are not limited to: • • • Pumping out the basin using a licensed septage hauler;

The current IBM Power9 system is more than five years old, and IBM will no longer provide maintenance support for most Power9 systems as of 12/31/26. Staff recommends replacing the current system with a new IBM Power11, which includes updated hardware and software, installation and migration services, and a five-year maintenance and support warranty. The existing system will be repurposed for Disaster Recovery, providing additional protection in the event of a system outage. The proposal also includes an automated digital backup system specifically designed for the AS/400 environment. The total project cost is $102,915. The County set aside $32,500 in FY26 and an additional $32,500 in FY27, leaving $37,915 to be funded from the Computer System line item. Staff recommends that the Board approve the $102,915 purchase and implementation. Attachments: CAS Severn Proposal Recommendation: See sample motion.
